d120e820108c347d: KUALA LUMPUR: The Intellectual Property Corporation of Malaysia (MyIPO) is stepping up efforts to help media practitioners understand intellectual property (IP) challenges in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly legal frameworks and content liability.
MyIPO director-general Yusnieza Syarmila Yusoff said a clear legal framework was crucial to educate industry players, especially on liability when AI platforms use content belonging to others.
"Charges for the use of intellectual property under the country's balance of payments account amounted to more than RM2 billion in 2024.

"When AI issues arise, the main question is who the liability should rest with if someone else's content snippets are used," she said at a forum held in conjunction with the 2026 National Intellectual Property Commercialisation Conference and Exhibition.
The forum was organised in collaboration with the Malaysian Press Institute (MPI).
Yusnieza said proposed amendments to the Copyright Act, expected to be tabled in parliament next year, would be an important benchmark in strengthening protection for creative works in Malaysia.
Meanwhile, New Straits Times Senior News Editor Robin Stanley Augustin said editors carry a heavy mandate in safeguarding newsroom integrity and compliance with intellectual property guidelines.
"If you are unsure of the source of content, do not share it, or seek permission and credit the original owner.
"In the era of AI, deepfake content and synthetic information, media practitioners must defend the truth and accuracy of facts," he said.
He added that NST used AI for tasks such as transcription and translation, but not to write stories, with editors remaining the gatekeepers.
He added that any video whose authenticity was in doubt would not be uploaded.

Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry Enforcement Division deputy director-general (operations) Shamsul Nizam Khalil said the division would work with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission to enforce Section 263 of the Communications and Multimedia Act for website blocking, besides content removal channels.
"Firm enforcement is carried out to protect content owners, as well as to safeguard the nation's competitiveness ratings and foreign direct investment," he said.
The session was attended by MPI president Datuk Yong Soo Heong and about 50 media practitioners and editors.
c80c9d0df2b1ace7: KUALA LUMPUR: Men's singles Lee Zii Jia stormed into the Arctic Open main draw in Finland after negotiating the qualifying round without trouble on Tuesday.

cb2da0cf4849a6e2: KULIM: An 11-year-old schoolgirl was found hiding in a school toilet here today after a classmate falsely claimed she had left the school with a man on a motorcycle.

Kulim district police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring said the incident began around 9.20am when a student told a teacher that her classmate had left the school compound with an unidentified man on a motorcycle.
The teacher, who is also the senior assistant for student affairs, informed the girl's parents before lodging a report at Sungai Kob police station.
Syamsul said the girl had arrived at school at 7.20am after being dropped off by her sister and attended the 8am assembly.
"During the assembly, she played with a classmate's hair bun. The classmate responded by pulling her headscarf, causing her inner cap to fall off," he said in a statement today.
He said the girl, upset by the incident, went to the toilet after assembly to adjust her headscarf but decided to hide there instead of returning to class.
"When she failed to appear in class, another pupil told the teacher that she had left the school compound with a man on a motorcycle," he said.
However, the pupil later admitted fabricating the story out of resentment towards the girl.
Syamsul said the classmate who had pulled the girl's headscarf knew the story was false but went along with it.
"Investigations confirmed that the girl never left the school premises and remained in the toilet throughout the incident," he said.
The girl's aunt said the family had been deeply worried about her safety and was relieved that she was found safe.
The 'disappearance' had earlier gone viral on social media, with members of the public urged to help locate the pupil.
fa2d62086bf51bf2: JOHOR BARU: The widening gap between Singapore salaries and Johor living costs has created a lucrative cross-border equation for workers, with the trend increasingly spilling into the state capital's property market.
For Malaysians earning Singapore dollars but living in Johor, the appeal is straightforward: earn in a stronger currency, pay rent and daily expenses in ringgit and retain more disposable income.
In February, Human Resources Minister R. Ramanan said more than 1.18 million Malaysians were estimated to be working in Singapore, with about 400,000 commuting daily across the Causeway.

The draw is clear: Singapore offers significantly higher wages and stronger career opportunities, while living in Johor allows workers to take advantage of Malaysia's lower housing and daily living costs.
However, the Singapore-Johor Baru salary arbitrage comes with a price - hours spent crossing the Causeway, transport costs, border congestion and the physical toll of commuting.
According to employment platform Hiredly, a worker earning about S$4,000 (RM13,200) a month could potentially save RM4,000 to RM5,000 monthly by living in Johor Baru rather than renting in Singapore.
The comparison puts a one-bedroom rental in Singapore at about RM7,500 to RM10,000 a month, against roughly RM1,200 to RM2,000 for an apartment in Johor Baru.
Even after factoring in about RM600 to RM900 in toll and commuting costs, the lower cost base in Johor could leave the worker with significantly greater spending power.
That has increasingly made areas such as Iskandar Puteri attractive to Singapore-linked workers, investors and landlords betting on sustained cross-border demand.

Property data cited by industry players showed two-bedroom condominiums in Iskandar Puteri rising from about RM250,000-RM350,000 in 2020 to RM380,000-RM550,000 this year, while comparable monthly rents had climbed from about RM900-RM1,400 to RM1,400-RM2,200.

The expected opening of the Johor-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link in February next year has further strengthened expectations that locations with convenient access to Singapore will command a premium.
However, the arbitrage is not simply a property story.
The daily journey across the Causeway can turn a seemingly attractive salary equation into a costly trade-off in time and quality of life, particularly for workers travelling during peak periods.
The emergence of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) could also alter the equation by creating more high-value jobs within Johor itself.

The zone is intended to attract Singapore-linked and multinational investments, while incentives for eligible knowledge workers and the Forest City Special Financial Zone (FC-SFZ) could further strengthen Johor's proposition as a lower-cost base for internationally linked businesses and workers.

The result could be a gradual shift in Johor Baru's housing market, namely from a city offering cheaper accommodation to a strategic residential base for workers whose incomes are linked to Singapore.
But whether the salary arbitrage remains compelling will ultimately depend on one calculation: how much is the worker willing to pay in time to save in ringgit?
ff22490d2e70f5f5: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuching City make their Asean Club Championship (ACC) debut against Tampines Rovers on Wednesday, with coach Aidil Sharin Sahak refusing to let a gruelling nine-match spell away from home become an excuse.
The Cats have not returned to Kuching during the run, which also saw them juggle Super League, FA Cup and AFC Champions League 2 (ACL 2) commitments.
Aidil admitted the demanding schedule had taken a toll on his players and affected their performances to some extent, but said the recent international break had given them valuable time to recover.
"As I said, it is not easy. But I will not make excuses. When we play, we will give our best," he said.
Kuching face Tampines at Taha Ariffin Stadium in Petra Jaya in their first appearance at Asean level, with Aidil saying the experience would be part of the club's learning process.
"This is the first time Kuching City are playing at the Asean level and we have to face all these challenges. I hope the fans will be patient with this team because this team is still new," he said.

Despite the challenges, Aidil believes Kuching remain in a strong position in all three competitions, with the team currently second in the Super League while their ACL 2 and FA Cup campaigns are still alive.
"In the Super League, we are still in second place. In the ACL 2, our chances are still open. Likewise, in the FA Cup, we are still in it and still have an advantage.
"This is the journey we have to go through and we will learn from it. I believe that through learning, we will become better," he said.
Aidil now wants his players to put the fatigue behind them and focus on Tampines as they look to make a winning start to their ACC campaign.
He also called for greater support from Kuching fans as the club takes on a new challenge at Asean level.
"At this time, we need the fans more than usual. Football will have no meaning without the supporters.
"Previously, nobody talked about Kuching City, but now we are here and we are doing our best. I don't think we have done anything wrong and we have nothing to lose," he said.
05fc44600610d360: KUALA LUMPUR: OCK Group Bhd has agreed in-principle to develop telecommunications infrastructure for selected Sun Group projects in Vietnam.

OCK, through its subsidiary VNC-55 Infrastructure Investment Co Ltd, signed a tripartite in-principle agreement with Southern Star Telecommunication Equipment Joint Stock Company (SPN), a subsidiary of JTower, and Sun Phu Quoc, a subsidiary of Sun Group.
OCK said the agreement covers cooperation, investment and deployment of telecommunications infrastructure across designated Sun Group projects in Phu Quoc.

The initial phase involves an investment of 13 billion dong (about RM2 million), with deployment expected to be completed and the infrastructure operational within six to 12 months from project commencement.
The projects include convention and media facilities, hotels, residential developments and airport-related works, including facilities supporting the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) 2027.
Under the cooperation framework, OCK will be responsible for all built-to-suit infrastructure and fibre networks within the agreed project scope, while SPN will oversee in-building solutions.
Sun Phu Quoc will participate as the project owner and developer.
For APEC 2027, the collaboration will combine outdoor mobile infrastructure, fibre connectivity and in-building coverage to support the event's connectivity requirements and longer-term needs.
OCK said the partnership provides an opportunity to expand its infrastructure investment in Vietnam and deepen its relationship with Sun Group across multiple developments.

The investment period is 20 years, during which OCK will have exclusive rights to operate the built-to-suit infrastructure and fibre networks, while SPN will have exclusive rights to operate the in-building infrastructure within the agreed project scope.
Details of subsequent phases are expected to be finalised over the coming months.

54e822756430c1fb: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 6 — A company director and a factory worker claimed trial in the Magistrate’s and Sessions Courts here today to charges including the theft of a lorry, dangerous driving, obstructing a police officer and drug possession.
Chai Min Quan, 39, and Low Boon Lai, 37, pleaded not guilty after the lorry theft charge was read to them in Malay by a court interpreter before Magistrate A. Shaarmini.

According to the charge, the two men allegedly stole a CD45-model lorry belonging to Max Theu Zhi Wei from a parking area in front of the BHP Plentong petrol station along Jalan Mutiara 4, Taman Plentong, Masai, near here, at 7.40am on September 30.
They were charged under Section 379A of the Penal Code for motor vehicle theft, which carries a prison term of between one and seven years and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Eizlan Azhar prosecuted, while Chai was represented by lawyer Yap Che Kai. Low was unrepresented.
The court set October 23 for the submission of documents and for Low to appoint a lawyer.

Both men were granted bail of RM7,000 each, with additional conditions requiring them to report to a nearby police station, surrender their international passports and refrain from interfering with the victim or witnesses.
Separately, Low pleaded not guilty before Magistrate Atifah Hazimah Wahab to two further charges, which were read to him in Mandarin.

On the first charge, he is accused of intentionally obstructing Corporal Muhammad Nazmi Ihsan Abdullah from carrying out his duties within the jurisdiction of the Pasir Putih police station at 8.25am on September 30.
He was charged under Section 186 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum prison term of two years, a fine of up to RM10,000, or both, upon conviction.
On the second charge, Low is accused of possessing 0.7g of methamphetamine by the roadside along Jalan Mawar Biru in the Pasir Gudang Industrial Area at 10.20am on the same day.
The charge was framed under Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, which carries a maximum prison term of five years, a fine of up to RM10,000, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Siti Aisyah Mustapha Kamal prosecuted, while Low was unrepresented.
The court set October 23 for the submission of documents in the obstruction case and granted Low bail of RM3,500.
Magistrate Atifah set December 7 for the submission of the chemistry report in the drug possession case and granted him bail of RM3,000.
In a related case, Low pleaded not guilty before Magistrate Nur Fatin Mohamad Farid to a charge of dangerous driving, which was also read to him in Mandarin.
He is accused of driving against the flow of traffic and making an illegal U-turn in a manner that endangered the public along Jalan Mawar Biru at 10.20am on September 30.

He was charged under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum five-year prison term and a fine of RM5,000, as well as the revocation of his driving licence upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by Johor Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department prosecuting officer Inspector S. Vikineswary. Low was unrepresented.
The court set November 5 for the submission of documents and granted him bail of RM5,000.
Last Wednesday, footage circulated on social media showing a man driving a lorry dangerously while fleeing several police patrol cars.
Police later said they had pursued the lorry for about two hours over a distance of 100 kilometres after two suspects allegedly stole the heavy vehicle in Plentong.
02b1b3bccd8fc1c9: KUALA LUMPUR: Reports and views from academics on the implementation of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) will be submitted to the Cabinet, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.

Fahmi, who is also the Madani government spokesman, said the government welcomed academics' involvement in assessing and providing constructive criticism on the implementation of the country's development plan.

"I believe the input, recommendations, views and constructive criticism that can be provided by our academic colleagues are important to be considered not only by the Economy Ministry, but by every ministry.

"So, I welcome the efforts by INPUMA (Institute of Public Policy and Management), Universiti Malaya, and I have asked that, if possible, they prepare a report which I can subsequently submit to the cabinet," he said after launching the 13th Malaysia Plan Public Discourse Conference: Direction and Challenges organised by INPUMA.
Fahmi said the implementation of 13MP projects must have good governance and be free from corruption to ensure that allocations were used effectively for the benefit of the people.

"In my speech, I stressed that we need to ensure that, as every Malaysia Plan is implemented using public funds, the implementation of projects under the 13th Malaysia Plan, in particular, must ensure proper governance, with no abuse of power or funds, as well as no kleptocracy or corruption and so on," he said.

On the Budget to be tabled on Friday, Fahmi said that on behalf of the Communications Ministry, he hoped the Finance Ministry would consider a new focus relating to the development of the 'orange economy'.
"This is because we have established an Orange Economy Council to look into the development of the creative economy, covering film, animation, music, as well as arts and culture.
"So, on behalf of the Communications Ministry, there are several matters that we have put forward and we hope they will be considered by the Finance Ministry," he said.

The conference aimed to obtain perspectives from various stakeholders on current economic and social issues affecting the country and the people, as well as identify concerns and needs that should be addressed in the implementation of the 13MP.
7e6e228a564e4686: PHNOM PENH, Oct 6 — Lao police have seized 521 kilogrammes of crystal methamphetamine from a private jet reported to have arrived from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport, with 13 people detained in connection with the case.

The Vientiane Times, citing Lao Security Newspaper, reported on Tuesday that a security operation took place on October 1 following a tip-off received by provincial police on September 21 that a drug trafficking syndicate was allegedly planning to smuggle narcotics across borders by air using a private aircraft.

According to the report, police later learned that the flight schedule had been changed, with the private aircraft due to arrive from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport at 1.30pm on October 1.
Provincial public security authorities then instructed specialised units to monitor the situation.

Officers subsequently found 23 suitcases and seized 500 packs of crystal methamphetamine weighing 521 kilogrammes, along with the Learjet private aircraft and a pickup truck as evidence, according to the report.
“Twenty-one of the 23 suitcases contained white crystalline substances that were identified as crystal methamphetamine,” the report said.

Police detained 13 people during the operation, including the pilot, co-pilot, a foreign tourist, three employees of a company and seven employees of Luang Prabang International Airport. Three of those detained were women.
The seized aircraft was identified as a Learjet with flight registration N73GP. — Bernama
c54e7f883daf627e: MELAKA, Oct 6 — Day-trippers and weekend tourists to Melaka flock to Jonker Street for the historical city’s iconic chicken rice balls and Nyonya laksa.
This is almost a given, though some venture a little farther to Tengkera and Bukit Cina too.
But wander beyond the town centre, and you might be surprised to discover pockets of Malaccan food havens.

From unassuming platters of chicken rice balls in Taman Pertam Jaya to unapologetically rich Nyonya laksa in Taman Sin Hoe, those willing to go outside the default tourist trails are often well rewarded with new spots where locals eat.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Suukee is located in Melaka’s Ayer Keroh industrial park. — Picture by CK Lim

Which might be how we find ourselves in Ayer Keroh, usually the last neighbourhood before one reaches the highway toll to exit the state (or the first when one enters, depending on how you look at it).
Specifically we are in Melaka’s Ayer Keroh industrial park, hardly the most promising of locations for browsing for bites. Or is it?
Factories are full of employees, all hungry during their lunch breaks and perhaps less than willing to travel too far.
Hungry and no appetite for fussy fare. They crave belly-sticking food, not an Instagram opportunity.

This is the mindset we adopted when our plate of chicken rice arrives. We are at Suukee, a local restaurant smack in the middle of the industrial park, and this is their signature kampung chicken rice.
They have a substance-over-style approach; this dish wouldn’t look out of place in a kopitiam.

Indeed, Suukee used to operate in Ayer Keroh Heights not far away; its new location does feel fancier with laminated menus, air-conditioning and a beverage station that wouldn’t look out of place in an upscale café.

But the food is served as is, without much fanfare. This is a good sign, to be honest; it shows confidence in the quality of what they offer and indeed the kampung chicken tastes naturally sweet, with a tender yet springy bite.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Suukee also offers chicken rice balls. — Picture by CK Lim

The oil rice is aromatic, and Suukee also offers this in the form of chicken rice balls. These are hefty, decent-sized orbs so be careful how many you attempt as the grains are compacted; your eyes might be bigger than your belly.
What to drink? Well, the coffee menu stays true to Suukee’s kopitiam style origins so you’d be safe ordering any of their kopi variations.
We tried the recommended kopi C with butter, which was suitably creamy and way more caffeinated than we imagined.
If you’re worried about your sleep later in the evening, you can try some of their different chicken soups with red dates.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
'Kopi C' with butter. — Picture by CK Lim
The old cucumber and the lotus root options are very old school, like grandma’s cooking.
Or simply stick with the bowl of clear soup that comes with your chicken rice; light and healing.
Don’t forget the piquant chilli sauce; it completes every spoonful of chicken rice.
There are other poultry delights, from braised chicken feet with mushrooms to crispy fried chicken intestines. But Suukee isn’t just about chicken rice.
This being Melaka, Peranakan dishes are an essential part of the restaurant’s revamped menu.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Nyonya 'laksa' with Hainanese 'kampung' chicken. — Picture by CK Lim
Try the Nyonya mee siam with ayam berempah or the Nyonya laksa with Hainanese steamed kampung chicken.
The latter is particularly soul-satisfying. First we got a punchy hit of the laksa’s curry paste and spices. Then there’s the broth itself, full of santan that creamily coats our lips.

What takes it to the next level is the topping of sliced kampung chicken (yes, it’s clear this is their specialty), the springy meat offering a textural and flavour contrast to the more decadent Nyonya laksa.
We finish our meal with some Cantonese style tong sui: the ebony of black glutinous rice and red bean soup and the ivory of the peanut and sticky rice porridge. Nothing like a sweet ending, no?
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Black glutinous rice and red bean 'tong sui'. — Picture by CK Lim

Zon Industri Ayer Keroh Baru, Melaka.
Open daily 10am-9pm

c37dd251c8c35105: SINGAPORE, Oct 6 — A 32-year-old man will be charged with murder following an incident at a Housing Board block in Telok Blangah Heights that left one man dead and another injured, police said today.
CNA reported that police said they received calls for assistance at about 6pm in the vicinity of Block 61 Telok Blangah Heights and arrived at the scene within 10 minutes.

Officers found a 73-year-old man lying motionless and a 53-year-old man injured on the ground floor of the block. Both were taken to Singapore General Hospital, where the older man later died from his injuries. The 53-year-old was conscious when conveyed to hospital.
Authorities said the suspect later contacted the police to surrender himself and was subsequently arrested nearby.
Investigators believe the man acted alone and said there is currently no indication that the incident was linked to terrorism or motivated by religion.
The suspect is expected to be charged on Wednesday under Section 302(1) of Singapore’s Penal Code. A murder conviction carries the death penalty.
64c8aa7272839624: Sweden is the home of bork, and what better way to mark it than with a huge example of digital signage that shows a GRUB message instead of an ad? Spotted by eagle-eyed Register reader Alexander, the GRUB in question is sadly not the delicious meatballs for which a well-known Swedish furniture maker is famed, but rather the bootloader familiar to Linux fans, usually when something is working as it should (since we can't imagine much call for selecting from multiple operating systems in the world of digital signage). GNU GRUB (the GRUB is short for Grand Unified Bootloader), according to GNU, "is responsible for loading and transferring control to the operating system kernel software." In this case, the user has some options. UEFI firmware is one. Some options for DMS are another. DMS might mean Dank Material Shell, unless you know better. It's an attractive enough desktop, but it seems like overkill for something that slings ads for the few seconds Stockholm commuters raise their gaze from their devices. Some enticing possibilities are on offer. Hitting "e" will edit the commands while "c" will drop the user into the command line. That's assuming, of course, that the user is carrying a keyboard to attach to the stricken screen, something we're sure every Register reader has in their backpack, but not something civilians would necessarily keep on their person. GRUB has featured in this column before, appearing on a UK bus after a filesystem became a bit poorly (motion sickness can clearly affect computers as well as commuters), but this is a wall-sized example of the breed. Judging by the passengers on the escalators opposite, it appears that nobody is rushing to the aid of the stricken signage. That's probably for the best – leave it for a few seconds (by the looks of things), and it'll have another go at booting. Still, it's always good to see GRUB putting in an appearance in a section often dominated by Windows and Android whoopsies. The era of the Linux desktop might not be upon us just yet, but judging by this Stockholm signage, bork is alive and kicking in the open-source world. ®
a9dded6844f32d95: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 6 — The Year Four Learning Matrix (MPT4) gives schools a crucial two-year window to address learning gaps through targeted interventions before students enter secondary school.
Examination Board (LP) director Abdul Aziz Mamat said the assessment was designed to help teachers identify and address students’ weaknesses as early as Year Five.

He said the assessment data would enable schools to implement targeted interventions, such as strengthening teaching and learning (PdP) processes, providing remedial support to students who have yet to master basic skills, and offering enrichment activities for those who have already mastered them.

“This gives us at least two years at the primary school level to implement intervention programmes to improve students’ performance and abilities, while also nurturing the potential of those who have already met the established standards.

“This approach allows interventions to be implemented based on students’ needs, rather than comparisons between students or schools,” he said in a video recording shared by the Ministry of Education (MOE) on X today.
MPT4, which is being implemented for the first time this year, involves more than 400,000 Year Four pupils nationwide and will run for three days until Thursday.
The assessment covers four core subjects, namely Bahasa Melayu, English, Mathematics and Science, as well as Chinese and Tamil for pupils at Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan.
It is designed to assess pupils’ mastery of basic literacy, numeracy and scientific skills acquired from Year One to Year Four.

To ensure that the interventions do not remain merely “on paper”, Abdul Aziz said responsibility for monitoring and quality assurance was not borne solely by teachers, but was shared across all levels of the education system.

He said teachers were responsible for identifying learning needs and planning interventions, while school administrators were responsible for ensuring that follow-up measures were properly planned and implemented.

Abdul Aziz added that at the district and state levels, LP, together with the relevant MOE divisions, would conduct quality assurance to ensure support and interventions were implemented fairly and effectively. — Bernama
c5cc79c9bd5bdd6c: TANJUNG MALIM: Watching a pantomime depicting the assassination of her father brought back painful memories for Datin Rita Koo, nearly 51 years after former Perak police chief Tan Sri Khoo Chong Kong was gunned down in Ipoh.
Koo, 78, the eldest of Khoo's five children, said she was deeply touched that the police continued to remember her father's sacrifice.

"Yes, it brought back all the memories and I felt very touched. The police remembered him and reminded us of his sacrifice," she said after attending the opening of the new Muallim district police headquarters (IPD).
The new IPD Muallim was officially opened by Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah.
Koo said the family first learnt of the shooting through a police officer who called her while she was in Seremban.
"They could not give us many details, so all we could do was rush back to Ipoh," she said.
Koo, who was married and living in Seremban at the time, said her father was often away from home for extended periods because of his duties, particularly during his years with the Special Branch.
"He was always very busy. My mother was very tense sometimes because when he went out on operations, we did not know when he would come back.
"Sometimes he would be away for one or two months on operations. He spent many years in the Special Branch, so he dealt a lot with communist insurgents," said the mother of three.
Despite his demanding duties, Koo remembered Khoo as a loving and devoted father.
"He was a very good father. He might have been fierce in his work, but at home he was very fatherly. He was a loving father," she said.
Koo said her father's bravery, dedication to duty and adherence to his principles were qualities she continued to admire.
"His bravery and dedication to duty. He would not take any nonsense. He went by principle," she said.
Koo, who was 25 when her father was killed, said the family had continued to preserve memories of him over the years.
She said seeing his police uniform and the Volvo associated with him during today's event also brought back memories of her childhood.
"Yes, definitely. It brought me back to those times. Although, in between, I have seen the car at the museum," she said.
Koo also said Sultan Nazrin took an interest in the family when he met them during the ceremony.
"He asked how the family was doing and what we were doing now. He was very interested in the family, where we are and what careers we are in," she said.
Khoo was gunned down at a traffic-light junction between Fair Park and Jalan Anderson in Ipoh on Nov 13, 1975 and died from his injuries the following day.
The pantomime, staged as part of the opening ceremony, depicted the attack and served as a poignant reminder of Khoo's service and sacrifice to the police force and country.
Khoo joined the police force in Sarawak in 1952 and served in various positions before rising through the ranks. He was appointed Perak police chief in 1975.
He placed strong emphasis on the welfare of police personnel. His firm stance against the communist threat resulted in him receiving death threats.
Despite threats to his safety and that of his family, Khoo remained committed to his duties.
About nine months after his appointment as Perak police chief, Khoo was attacked while travelling in an official police vehicle.

At noon on Nov 13, 1975, he was on his way home when the vehicle stopped at a traffic-light junction. A motorcycle carrying two men, disguised as school students, approached the vehicle before they opened fire.
Khoo was shot in the attack while his driver returned fire in an attempt to protect him.
Khoo was rushed to hospital and remained in critical condition for about 28 hours before dying on Nov 14, 1975.
His police uniform and the Volvo car used during the incident were also displayed during today's event.
Khoo's sacrifice continues to be remembered as a testament to the courage and dedication of police personnel in protecting the people and maintaining national security.

6da9ecbd5eb27e99: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises.

Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK).

“From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises,” he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank here today.

Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule.
He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce JBPM’s workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises.

“In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by JBPM for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year,” he said.
Nor Hisham said to meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, JBPM expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide.
He said JBPM currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors.
A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony. — Bernama
7ca4958ac3ec7305: BEIJING: American tennis star Coco Gauff said Tuesday she faced an "insane" amount of online racist abuse after defeating Chinese teenager Sun Xinran in a match that included a video review.
During Monday's China Open match against 16-year-old Sun Xinran in Beijing, the former US Open champion requested a video review over flickering LED lights, prompting some boos from the crowd.
"Hey everyone, you can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist," Gauff wrote on X.
"The amount of racist comments and messages I've received in the last few hours is insane," her post read.
The umpire agreed for the point to be replayed, and 22-year-old Gauff went on to win the match 7-5, 6-1.

Responding on X to a post containing a racial slur that was flagged as potential "hateful content", the Black American player clarified in a separate post that she challenged the point before Sun's return when she noticed the lights flicker a second time.
"I think it's weird I'm getting hate for following the rules," she said, explaining that players are instructed they can challenge points after play has concluded.
"Xinran is an incredible talent and player. I apologised for the situation at the end of the match, and she completely understood," she added.
By Tuesday morning, the hashtag "Gauff apologised to Sun Xinran after the match" had hit 4.5 million views, ranking as the sixth top trend on Chinese social media platform Weibo.
The Women's Tennis Association (WTA) did not immediately respond to AFP.
During a quarter-final match between Alexander Zverev and Novak Djokovic in the men's draw on Sunday, the umpire also agreed to replay a point after Zverev complained about flickering panels.
Gauff, the world No. 4, claimed the Beijing title in 2024. She is due to play Belgium's Elise Mertens in the round of 16 on Wednesday. - AFP
8c7a8004f2c6ac39: KUALA LUMPUR: The youth and sports minister should seek advice from experienced athletes before taking action against sports bodies, Tebrau MP Jimmy Puah said today.

Puah said there were concerns about "absolute power" being given to the minister under the proposed Section 41A of the Sports Development (Amendment) Bill 2026 to declare a sports body unlawful and revoke its registration.
He suggested that the minister seek the views of experienced athletes, citing badminton great Lee Chong Wei and squash champion Nicol David as examples.
"Like it or not, we have to admit that athletes are the ones who brought pride to our country's name for decades.

"Therefore, it is crucial that the minister seek those who are experienced so that any decision always prioritises the athletes that we are trying to develop," he said while debating the Sports Development (Amendment) Bill 2026 in the Dewan Rakyat.

Nevertheless, Puah welcomed the proposed amendments to the Sports Development Act, saying they could reduce red tape in the distribution of aid to athletes and coaches. He also urged the government to make further improvements to the mechanism.
"We need to ensure that the existing (awarding) mechanism is improved so that incentives, facilities and aid really reach the people who are delivering results, namely athletes and coaches.
"They are the real people that we should be supporting," he said.
Meanwhile, Afnan Hamimi Taib Azamudden (PN-Alor Setar) urged the government to consider introducing an athletes’ rights charter as part of the sports development framework.
He said athletes should have the right to clear information on the programmes they join, the offers made to them and decisions affecting them within a reasonable timeframe.
They should also have their welfare and safety protected, as well as access to fair channels for complaints and dispute resolution, he said.
"Don't leave our athletes hanging without certainty about their future," he said, adding that the bill was generally good but lacked clear mention of athletes' rights.

Earlier today, youth and sports minister Dr Taufiq Johari tabled the amendment bill under which sports bodies used for purposes harmful to national security, public order or morality can be declared unlawful by the minister and immediately struck off.

Under the proposed Section 41A, the minister may, after consulting the sports commissioner, issue a gazetted order against any sports body "used for purposes harmful to national security, public order or morality".
The bill also creates an enforcement and investigation regime, giving ministry-appointed enforcement officers and police the power to record statements and seize documents from sports bodies.
67044f4a3e5a7456: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 6 — The repatriation of Myanmar refugees will continue once the 5,000 individuals agreed upon by the Myanmar government have been sent home, said Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban.
Speaking at a press conference on a special operation here today, Zakaria said 1,476 individuals were repatriated in the first phase last month, while more than 3,000 remain in the country.
“This is an ongoing process. It does not stop at just these 5,000. We have not set a quota. If possible, we want them all to return,” he said.

Based on UNHCR (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees) records of issued cards, the number of registered refugees in the country now exceeds 200,000, with nearly half estimated to be Myanmar nationals, he said.
On September 29, Malaysia carried out the first phase of the repatriation programme involving 1,476 Myanmar detainees aboard three vessels, including a Myanmar Navy hospital ship.
The repatriated group comprised 1,370 men, 79 women, 20 boys and seven girls, aged between eight and 60.
Zakaria said the Immigration Department is still awaiting feedback from Wisma Putra regarding further negotiations with the Myanmar authorities for the second phase.
Meanwhile, Zakaria said the exact number of refugees in Malaysia has yet to be determined, and the department is relying on data from UNHCR-issued cardholders.

“I cannot give an estimate, which is why we are implementing the DPP (Refugee Registration Document). The main purpose of the DPP is to determine the actual number of refugees in our country,” he said.
Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah was previously reported as saying that the DPP, the official registration system for refugees, was implemented early this year.
The initiative was carried out to address security risks and irregular data issues, in line with National Security Council Directive No. 23. — Bernama
8f40aa2677e59ef7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — A24’s psychological thriller Primetime has been banned in Malaysia by the Film Censorship Board (Lembaga Penapis Filem, or LPF), local distributor Antenna Entertainment announced today.
In a statement posted on X, Antenna expressed regret to local moviegoers, confirming that the film “will not be released in Malaysia.”
“Unfortunately, the film has been BANNED by Lembaga Penapis Filem (LPF),” the distributor said in its post.
“We sincerely apologise for any disappointment and thank everyone for your support and interest in PRIMETIME.”

Leading cinema chain Golden Screen Cinemas (GSC) separately confirmed the cancellation on X, notifying patrons that the title would no longer see a Malaysian release, though the exhibitor’s post did not explicitly reference the censorship ban.
Neither Antenna nor GSC disclosed the specific grounds behind the censorship board’s prohibition. The LPF has yet to issue a public statement explaining the decision.
The ban follows an earlier release postponement announced on Sept 19 by Antenna and TGV Cinemas, which had initially shifted the film’s Malaysian debut from Oct 1 to Oct 8.
That earlier notice apologised for the scheduling change while teasing an unspecified “something in the works” for Oct 2, the nature of which remains unconfirmed.

Directed by Lance Oppenheim in his narrative feature debut, Primetime stars Robert Pattinson, who also serves as a producer. The film features Pattinson portraying a fictionalized television host inspired by Chris Hansen of NBC’s reality show To Catch a Predator.

The ensemble cast includes Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo, and singer-songwriter Phoebe Bridgers. The screenplay draws inspiration from a 2007 Esquire investigative feature documenting the controversial behind-the-scenes production of the reality television series.
The film made its world premiere in competition at the Venice International Film Festival on Sept 5 before opening across North American cinemas on Sept 25.
e03030ad95ed706b: KUALA LUMPUR: Efforts to determine the fate of 54 Malaysians still missing in Nepal must continue despite the country's decision to halt search operations, says Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH).

MASFIH spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said that while the organisation respected Nepal's jurisdiction and decision to end the active search phase, families still urgently needed answers about their loved ones.
"The transition from search and rescue to recovery must be accompanied by continued efforts to provide the answers these families need," he said when contacted today.
"We understand that Nepal's decision was based on ground assessments, safety concerns, accessibility and recommendations from the relevant authorities."
Nepal ended its search operations after 40 days as the prospects of finding survivors diminished significantly.

The decision followed recommendations from the District Security Committee, District Disaster Management Committee and National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, as well as field inspections.

A National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council meeting chaired by Prime Minister Balendra Shah also directed agencies to accelerate reconstruction and recovery efforts while maintaining only essential search operations.
As of Oct 3, the disaster had claimed 1,455 lives, with 5,285 people still missing.
Manivannan said many families were devastated and struggled to accept news that the official search had been called off.
"It is difficult for them to accept this news. They still hold on to hope for the return of their loved ones, making the termination of search operations very painful to understand," he said.
"Some check their phones every day, waiting for a call or message that might bring news of their family members."
Manivannan, whose sister Komathi Rethinam remains among the missing, said he was also awaiting news of her.

In a related development, he said MASFIH had requested that 20 additional DNA samples from a group of 23 Malaysians who travelled together be submitted to Chinese authorities for matching, subject to procedural clearance.
Three DNA samples from the group had previously been submitted to Chinese authorities for matching.
8242272cf18c4267: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Some 200 auxiliary police personnel will be deployed at East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) hotspots from November as part of tighter security measures against cable theft and to ensure smooth rail operations.

Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak said detection devices, alarm systems and closed-circuit television cameras had also been installed, while security guards and enforcement agencies were being engaged.

“Throughout the construction of the ECRL, we suffered losses of about RM4 million due to cable theft, including three cases last month,” he said at an ECRL operational readiness briefing for media editors today.
Darwis said MRL, as the project and asset owner, remained confident that the ECRL could begin operations by mid-December 2026, based on positive results from System Integration Testing (SIT).

He said progress in the testing and commissioning phase had allowed Fault-Free Runs (FFR) involving Electric Multiple Units (EMUs) for passenger services and electric locomotives (E-Locos) for freight services to begin this month, a month ahead of schedule, without compromising safety or quality.
Meanwhile, Darwis welcomed the agreement between the governments of Malaysia and China on the proposed 30km extension of the ECRL from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang.
He said the extension was expected to reuse about 18km of Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) tracks between Pasir Mas and Rantau Panjang, which have been out of service since 2005.
“The project will facilitate the movement of cargo from southern Thailand to Malaysia, while allowing us to explore the potential of extending the line,” he said.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the proposed extension following his recent working visit to China, saying it could connect Malaysia’s rail network with Thailand’s east coast rail system and strengthen links within the wider Pan-Asian rail network.

ECRL Operation Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Zaidi Sharif, meanwhile, said its E-Loco freight service had attracted strong interest from major companies seeking to reduce transport costs and their carbon footprint.
“The E-Loco service will not operate on a fixed timetable but according to demand from companies requiring freight services, which will operate at night,” he said. — Bernama
bcba9acd0c4bb72b: KUALA LUMPUR: M-pop trio Dolla have returned with their latest single, Ugly — a bold, high-energy track centred on self-worth, defiance, and refusing to be pushed aside.
Members Sabronzo, Angel, and Tabby describe the song as more than just entertainment.

It serves as a personal statement, transforming past feelings of rejection and judgment into creative strength. "If we had to describe Ugly in one word, it would be 'uncompromising'," the group shared in a recent statement, adding that the track encourages listeners to stand firm in their identity.
The accompanying music video takes visual cues from wayang kulit, Malaysia's traditional shadow puppetry.
By playing with light, shadow, and movement, the visual explores the stark contrast between perception and reality.

"We see shadows and jump to conclusions about a character without ever seeing the full picture," Dolla explained, noting how people often judge others based on assumptions, rumours, or surface appearances.
Looking ahead, the trio are eager to push their artistic boundaries, with plans to elevate their stage performances and reach an international audience.

e76207a0b662a135: A billion meals a year are wasted in this country. We need food businesses and government to make redistribution the default route Charlotte Hill is chief executive of the food redistribution organisation Felix How often does this happen? You open the fridge and find some ingredient you meant to use but didn’t get round to, and even though it’s still edible you think perhaps it’s just easier to throw it away. In the UK it’s estimated that an average household wastes about three meals a week, or 156 meals a year. Household fridges are one thing. But across the food sector more than 1bn meals’ worth of easily accessible surplus food is wasted each year in the UK for the same reason: because it is easier to throw it away. That equates to 470,000 tonnes – enough to feed every child in the UK three meals a day for a month. When so many people are struggling to afford food, that is a staggering amount, and what’s even more shocking is that it is good quality and nutritious. a52bbbb5f61673dc: Researchers argue incorrect binding of Voynich manuscript radically changes ideas about its drawings and indecipherable text It has been called the world’s most mysterious manuscript: a medieval set of pages filled with botanical drawings, astronomical diagrams, pictures of nude women and indecipherable text. Claimed at various times to be a book in a lost language, a musical score, an instruction manual or just an elaborate hoax, the so-called Voynich manuscript’s true meaning has defied cryptographers and codebreakers for centuries. 70edb3d180fff8ad: US televangelist Jim Bakker, who built a multimillion-dollar empire and lived in opulence before being disgraced by a sex scandal, fraud conviction for bilking followers and divorce from television co-host Tammy Faye, died on Monday at age 86.

The death of Bakker, whose journey from the TV pulpit to a prison cell in the 1980s inspired comparisons to the corrupt character of the fictional preacher-huckster Elmer Gantry, was revealed on social media by his second wife, Lori Bakker.

"It is with a broken heart that I share that my beloved husband, Jim Bakker, went home to be with the Lord this evening," she wrote on the Facebook and Instagram pages of her husband's latest television ministry.
She paid tribute to Bakker as a "pioneer of Christian television," but the cause and circumstances of his death were not revealed.

Bakker revived his career as a television preacher after prison with a new wife and new television show in 2003, later becoming a staunch supporter of President Donald Trump, who was known for his own brand of right-wing populism.

Bakker had been among the most popular of the Christian preachers who thrived on US television in the 1980s, achieving fame on the show "The PTL Club." PTL stood for "Praise The Lord" and "People That Love."
Detractors, pointing to his unabashed daily exhortations to viewers for donations to his ministry, said PTL should have stood for "pass the loot."

Bakker spent 4-1/2 years in prison after being convicted in Charlotte, North Carolina, in 1989 of defrauding followers in a scheme involving vacations at his Heritage USA Christian theme park and resort.
Prosecutors painted him as a selfish and petty con man driven by greed and lust for power.
"Those of us who do have a religion are sick of being saps for money-grubbing preachers and priests," Judge Robert Potter told Bakker before sentencing him.

Bakker had quit the PTL ministry in 1987 after revelations of a 1980 sexual encounter with Jessica Hahn, a former church secretary who later posed nude in Playboy magazine, and a subsequent US$265,000 payoff with ministry funds to gain her silence. Bakker was later defrocked.

Jim and Tammy Faye Bakker, his first wife, had started with a small TV ministry and eventually created a multimillion-dollar operation with 2,000 employees and the 930-hectare Heritage USA complex in Fort Mill, South Carolina.
At its peak, the PTL ministry drew 13 million viewers on 200 TV stations and raked in US$129 million a year.
With his working-class upbringing, the affable Bakker related well to common folk.
He did not deliver fire-and-brimstone sermons like other televangelists, instead offering a friendly Christian message - although it was larded with requests for money donations.
Tammy Faye was more much more flamboyant, with her enthusiastic singing and penchant for tears that left her heavy makeup smeared on her face.
Bakker was convicted after a six-week trial in federal court on all 24 fraud and conspiracy charges brought against him.
Prosecutors said he defrauded followers of US$158 million by selling promises of lifetime annual vacations that he could not provide.
They said he siphoned US$3.7 million to bankroll a lavish lifestyle that included several homes, luxury cars, mink coats, diamonds, servants - and an air-conditioned dog house.
The judge ordered Bakker to 45 years in prison but the sentence was later reduced. "I have sinned," Bakker told the court. "I have made mistakes. But never in my life did I intend to defraud anyone."
Bakker's chief aide, Richard Dortch, served 18 months of an eight-year prison sentence after pleading guilty to reduced charges in exchange for testifying against Bakker.
Tammy Faye was never charged. She stood by Bakker at the trial - even singing to reporters after his conviction - but divorced him in 1992 while he was in prison. She died of cancer in 2007.
Bakker started his life over after leaving prison in 1994, renouncing the "prosperity gospel" he once preached and writing a book titled "I Was Wrong."
"I've had a second chance at life. And I have a beautiful wife who loves me," Bakker told CNN in 2000, referring to his second wife, Lori, who he married in 1998.

They started a TV ministry together in 2003. In 2008, they began taping "The Jim Bakker Show" at a 600-acre (240-hectare) development called Morningside near the tourism city of Branson, Missouri, that bore similarities to Heritage USA.
Bakker once again pleaded with his followers for donations. In 2020, he drew the ire of state and federal officials for selling a false treatment for Covid-19 during the deadly coronavirus pandemic.
Bakker also said in 2017 that Christians would launch a civil war if Trump were to be impeached. Trump later became the first US president to be impeached twice.
James Orson Bakker was born on Jan 2, 1940, the son of an auto parts factory worker in Muskegon, Michigan, who maintained a strict fundamentalist Christian household.
He met Tammy Faye LaValley at North Central Bible College in Minneapolis and they married in 1961.
Both dropped out of school to become travelling evangelists as he pursued the career of a minister of the Pentecostalist Assemblies of God denomination.
Their big break came in 1964, when televangelist Pat Robertson aired a children's religious puppet show with them on his fledgling TV network.
Setting out on his own in the 1970s, Bakker used the emerging world of cable and satellite TV to build an empire.

5ef8e6ecd222e5aa: KUALA LUMPUR: Kang Khai Xing has accepted the challenge from national men's doubles head coach Herry IP to improve his speed and power in a bid to resume his partnership with Aaron Tai.

The former world junior champions are undergoing a reshuffle exercise, with Khai Xing having partnered Wan Arif Junaidi and currently with Lok Hong Quan, while Aaron has partnered Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik on the World Tour.
Khai Xing admitted he was a little disappointed when Herry split the pair, but the 20-year-old shuttler is ready to return as a physically stronger player in the hope of combining with Aaron again.

"I was a little disappointed (after splitting with Aaron). Over the past two or three weeks, I've been focusing on my physical condition — speed and power on court. So far, I feel that I've improved," said Khai Xing at the Academy Badminton Malaysia (ABM) on Tuesday.
"For now, I'm just focusing on myself first. If I'm not ready, there's no point in resuming the partnership with him."
While Khai Xing doesn't mind trying out with other players, he pointed out that his world ranking with Aaron is already No. 18 and could go to waste by starting from scratch.

"I'll continue trying. But our ranking is already quite high, so if we change partners, we have to start all over again from the Future Series, which will make it difficult. It (a permanent split) would be a huge waste," stressed Khai Xing.
Khai Xing will begin his first tournament with Hong Quan at the Malaysia Super 100 event in Iskandar Puteri next week.
Meanwhile, Aaron will partner Yap Roy King here, with the pair taking on Malaysian world No. 24 Nur Azriyn Ayub-Tan Wee Kiong in the first round of the Arctic Open in Vantaa, Finland, on Wednesday.
Aaron-Roy King will also compete in the French Open on Oct 20-25 and the Hylo Open on Oct 27-Nov 1.
c5a15a4c42d7e1e7: KUALA TERENGGANU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) will decide on its cooperation with other parties for the Melaka state election after the Election Commission (EC) announces the nomination date.
Its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the coalition would wait for the EC's announcement on Oct 7 before deciding on the matter.
"I will not comment now. Let us wait until Oct 7, after the EC announces the nomination date.
"I think all parties are also waiting for the dates to be announced by the EC," he said after the 2026 Terengganu Excellent Service Awards ceremony at Wisma Darul Iman.
On the number of seats PN would contest, Samsuri said seat allocation was still being discussed.

"There needs to be a formula for these discussions. If the formula is based on the status quo, I think it should take into account the status quo at both the state and federal levels, including parliamentary seats.
"Only then will we have a consistent formula to guide seat negotiations with any party," he said.
On the use of PN's logo, Samsuri said the coalition was awaiting a response from the Registrar of Societies (RoS).
"In our letter to RoS, we specifically asked about the use of PN's logo in the Melaka election.
"Perhaps RoS is also waiting for the election dates, so let us wait for its response first," he said.
eff32338554b8bda: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Jaya Grocer has warned customers not to respond to fake promotional posts offering gold bars, iPhones and other prizes after its Instagram account was compromised.
The supermarket chain said the posts, which purported to advertise an “Anniversary Promo” and directed users to a Telegram account, were not published by the company.
“Jaya Grocer is not running these promotions,” it said in a notice on its official Facebook page.
The company urged members of the public not to click on any links contained in the posts, contact the Telegram account or make any payments.
Those who have already responded to the posts were advised to contact their banks immediately and lodge a police report.
Jaya Grocer said it was working to regain control of its Instagram account and would issue further updates once available.
“We are working to regain control of the account and will provide updates as soon as possible,” it said.
3e2b5b1e721c4f12: NEW DELHI: The World Bank raised its growth forecast for South Asia, citing resilient consumer demand despite an energy shock, but warned that persistently high oil prices, a severe weather shock and a global market correction could threaten the region's outlook.

The Bank now expects the region to grow 6.9% in 2026, 60 basis points (bps) higher than its previous forecast and 10 basis points above its estimate a year ago as "higher energy prices have not interrupted momentum in consumption growth."

"This is because government measures to shield consumers, strong remittances and resilient domestic demand have helped cushion the impact," World Bank Chief Asia Economist Franziska Ohnsorge said in an interview with Reuters on Monday.
The region, heavily dependent on energy imports, has so far proved more resilient than expected to supply disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The Bank predicted India, the largest economy in the region, will grow 7.1% in 2026/27, up from the 6.6% it predicted in June but significantly lower than the 8.6% recorded in 2025/26.
Growth has held up even as higher inflation has eroded consumer purchasing power, a decoupling that has been "quite striking", Ohnsorge said.

"Inflation is expected to remain elevated into 2027," she said, adding it could take time for higher inflation to affect growth. "In emerging markets, the normal lag between such shocks and their effect on economic activity is around 18 months."
The Bank has not given a specific aggregate South Asia inflation forecast for 2026 but does provide country-level forecasts.

India's central bank expects inflation to average 5% in the current financial year and is expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points on October 7, its first increase since 2023, with another hike likely in December, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters.

A strong El Niño could pose another risk, particularly for India, where agriculture is key for rural demand and inflation, Ohnsorge said. India last experienced El Niño conditions in 2023, when monsoon rainfall was 95% of the long-period average.
The World Bank urged countries to adopt AI to maintain growth momentum over the medium term.

"One promising avenue for creating more, better jobs is the widespread deployment of AI. AI adoption in South Asia remains well behind that in advanced economies, but is catching up fast," the report said.
In India, which accounts for a large share of the region's economic expansion, some 23% of firms report using AI, against 43% of US firms.
bd0cfd8bb4b69099: PUTRAJAYA: Penghantaran pulang pelarian Myanmar akan diteruskan selepas 5,000 individu yang dipersetujui kerajaan Myanmar untuk diterima pulang selesai dihantar, kata Ketua Pengarah Imigresen Zakaria Shaaban.

Bercakap pada sidang media operasi khas di sini hari ini, Zakaria berkata setakat ini 1,476 individu telah dihantar pulang menerusi fasa pertama bulan lepas, manakala lebih 3,000 lagi masih berada di negara ini.
“Ini proses (penghantaran pulang) yang berterusan, bukan setakat 5,000 ini sahaja. Kita tidak ada tetapkan kuota. Kalau boleh kita nak semua balik.

“Berdasarkan rekod kad dikeluarkan UNHCR (Suruhanjaya Tinggi Pertubuhan Bangsa-Bangsa Bersatu), jumlah pelarian berdaftar dalam negara kini melebihi 200,000 orang dan dianggarkan hampir separuh daripada jumlah tersebut merupakan warga Myanmar,” katanya.

Pada 29 Sept, Malaysia melaksanakan program penghantaran pulang fasa pertama melibatkan 1,476 tahanan warga Myanmar menggunakan tiga kapal, termasuk sebuah kapal hospital milik Tentera Laut Myanmar, dengan semua individu terbabit terdiri daripada 1,370 lelaki, 79 wanita, 20 kanak-kanak lelaki dan tujuh kanak-kanak perempuan berusia antara lapan hingga 60 tahun.
Zakaria berkata bagi pelaksanaan fasa kedua, Imigresen masih menunggu maklum balas Wisma Putra, untuk rundingan lanjut dengan pihak berkuasa Myanmar.
“Kita (Malaysia) akan teruskan rundingan dengan kerajaan Myanmar,” katanya.
Dalam pada itu, Zakaria berkata jumlah pelarian di Malaysia masih belum dapat dikenal pasti secara tepat dan pihaknya bergantung kepada data pemegang kad yang dikeluarkan UNHCR.

“Saya tidak boleh bagi anggaran (jumlah), sebab itu kita laksanakan DPP (Dokumen Pendaftaran Pelarian). Tujuan utama DPP ini untuk kenal pasti berapa sebenarnya jumlah pelarian yang berada di negara kita,” katanya.
Timbalan Menteri Dalam Negeri Shamsul Anuar Nasarah sebelum ini dilaporkan berkata DPP iaitu sistem pendaftaran rasmi bagi pelarian di negara ini, telah dilaksanakan awal tahun ini.
Inisiatif itu dilaksanakan bagi menangani risiko keselamatan dan isu data yang tidak teratur selaras dengan arahan Majlis Keselamatan Negara (MKN) Nombor 23.

ae041537946a1bfc: SINGAPORE, Oct 6 — Eight public officers have been referred to the police following a government review into property purchases made near future MRT station sites before their locations were publicly announced, Singapore’s Public Service Division (PSD) revealed today.

The officers were among 191 individuals whose property transactions were scrutinised after questions emerged over whether civil servants may have benefited from access to confidential information related to rail development plans.

According to CNA, while addressing Parliament, Coordinating Minister for Public Services Chan Chun Sing said the majority of cases reviewed did not raise concerns, but eight transactions required further investigation due to unresolved issues surrounding the purchases.
He stressed that the police referrals should not be interpreted as proof of misconduct, noting that investigations would determine whether any rules had been breached.

The review was launched after an academic paper highlighted a pattern of property acquisitions near MRT stations before official announcements were made, raising concerns about possible insider knowledge.

Authorities examined transactions involving officers who worked in agencies connected to transport and rail planning, assessing whether they had access to non-public information at the time of their purchases and whether such information could have influenced buying decisions.
Chan said the exercise covered 2007 to 2014, extending beyond the period highlighted in the research to ensure a more comprehensive assessment.

While most cases were cleared, several could not be conclusively ruled out based on the information available to the government. Those cases were subsequently passed to the police for independent investigation.

The minister said maintaining public trust in the civil service was critical, adding that officers are expected to uphold strict standards of integrity and avoid using privileged information for personal gain.
He also indicated that the government would review whether existing safeguards governing confidential information and personal declarations remain adequate in light of the findings.
Questions over potential conflicts of interest have attracted public attention amid Singapore’s long-standing emphasis on clean governance and a corruption-free public sector.
The outcome of the police investigations is expected to determine whether any disciplinary or legal action will follow.
e60dcbb90c0fa3e9: KOTA KINABALU: Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) is targeting at least 14 of Sabah's 25 parliamentary seats in the next general election.

Its secretary-general Datuk Armizan Ali said the target was based on a simulation using the results of last year's state election, before United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation (Upko) joined the coalition.
"Based on the simulation, without taking into account the inclusion of Upko, GRS could, on paper, win 14 to 15 parliamentary seats.

"But we want more than that because we want Sabah to have a strong and solid voice through GRS, with a much larger number of seats," he told reporters after the six-party coalition's supreme council meeting at the Sabah International Convention Centre.
The meeting was chaired by Sabah Chief Minister and GRS chairman Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
Also present were the presidents of Parti Bersatu Sabah, Parti Cinta Sabah, Upko, Parti Harapan Rakyat Sabah and Liberal Democratic Party.
Armizan, who is a Papar member of parliament, said with the inclusion of Upko's two MPs, GRS now had seven MPs.
"We do not want to merely repeat the sentiment and support we received in the previous election. Fourteen seats are not sufficient. We want more than that.

"That is why our target and our work must be more strategic and focused — retaining our existing support base while increasing our strength so that we have one voice to advance Sabah's interests at the federal level.

"It is certainly not only about the seats that have the potential to be won. More importantly, the lessons learnt from the previous election, including the need to balance ourselves, are also important," he said.
Asked whether GRS would use the same formula as in the previous state election, Armizan said the coalition would listen to the views of Sabahans and study their aspirations.
At present, GRS is working with Barisan Nasional and independent assemblymen in the state government.
He said the coalition also had to take into account the need for unity and stability within the state administration, given its current composition.
"But we know that politics is very dynamic, especially now. That is why our priority at the moment is to strengthen GRS.
"We know that the political dynamics in Peninsular Malaysia among the major parties may also influence the shape of cooperation at the state level.

"Therefore, we want to ensure the stability of the state government continues. At the same time, we want the people's voice, through the state government, to be taken into account and not rejected," he said.
"Most importantly, we need to strengthen our own house first," he said.
Earlier, Armizan said GRS would hold its convention in Kudat on Oct 18, with about 2,500 people expected to attend.
Meanwhile, he said the meeting also heard views from component parties on the 2027 state budget.
"The chief minister gave the parties an opportunity to provide their initial views on what should be considered and included in the 2027 state budget.
"And it did not stop there. The GRS chairman also gave them more time to submit their proposals and views in writing to Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, who is also the finance minister," he said.

bae228f18031cba5: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — The role and responsibilities of the Peninsular Malaysia Orang Asli Advisory Council will be finalised through amendments to the Aboriginal Peoples Act 1954 (Act 134), which will be tabled in Parliament soon.

Deputy Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Rubiah Wang said the council currently operates as a committee that serves as an engagement platform between the government, the Orang Asli community, and relevant non-governmental organisations.
“The establishment (of the council) will be finalised in the amendments to the Aboriginal Peoples Act 1954 (Act 134), which we will table in Parliament in the near future.
“There, we will detail the role and responsibilities of the council in full,” she said during the Question-and-Answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

She was replying to a supplementary question from Abdul Latiff Abdul Rahman (PN-Kuala Krai) regarding the functions and jurisdiction of the council, as well as the steps taken by the government to ensure its views are translated into the formulation and enhancement of policies related to Orang Asli interests.

On the socio-economic development of the Orang Asli community, Rubiah said the Department of Orang Asli Development (JAKOA) provides entrepreneur grants ranging from RM9,000 to RM35,000. It also offers cooperative grants of up to RM200,000 to support business equipment and premises.
She added that the government also offers agricultural modernisation programmes with financing from RM5,000 to RM300,000. These programmes cover a broad range of assistance.
“In this regard, we hope the Orang Asli will continue submitting applications to ensure sustainable income generation and expand the local economy holistically,” she said. — Bernama
