8c794cb9f9da5dba: KUALA LUMPUR: Families of 54 Malaysians still unaccounted for following flash floods and landslides in Nepal have raised concerns over the handling of insurance matters, personal data and financial affairs linked to the missing individuals.

Spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the concerns emerged after several families were contacted by insurance adjusters claiming to have been appointed by an insurance company to verify information on the victims.

He said MASFIH sought clarification from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), which confirmed that the company had appointed adjusters to gather information and verify individuals who might have records with the insurer.

"However, according to the explanation received by MASFIH, of the 55 names received, four matched the insurance company's records, and the matter has not been finalised as a claim," Manivannan said in a statement today.
He said the adjusters had shown families an official letter from the insurer dated Sept 15 containing 15 names for investigation and verification.
Manivannan stressed that MASFIH was not concluding that all 15 were policyholders.

"However, the discrepancy between the 15 names listed in the official letter and the explanation that only four matched the company's records raises valid questions that need to be explained to the families," he said.
He questioned why 15 names were listed for verification if only four matched the insurer's records, as well as the actual scope and purpose of appointing the adjusters.
Manivannan said further concerns arose over the collection of personal data.
According to explanations received by MASFIH, the adjusters were asked to obtain the missing individuals' identity card numbers to allow the insurer to identify or match policy records.
"However, the insurance company's official letter dated Sept 15 shown to the families already contained the names, identity card numbers and passport numbers of the individuals listed," he said.
"If the identity card numbers were already in the letter, why did the adjusters still need to collect the same information from the families?"

He said that if further verification was required, families should be clearly informed of the reason, purpose, recipients, parties processing the data and how it would be protected under the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (Act 709).

MASFIH also called on BNM to clarify what regulatory checks or action were being taken, saying the families deserved to know whether any shortcomings or non-compliance were being addressed through the proper channels.
85fc35a3d5097db4: PETALING JAYA: Seramai 98 individu ditahan dalam serbuan di sebuah resort di Sungai Lembing, Pahang, yang ditutup sejak tahun lalu namun dipercayai dijadikan pangkalan operasi sindiket penipuan antarabangsa.

Ketua Pengarah Imigresen Zakaria Shaaban berkata mereka yang ditahan terdiri daripada 95 warga asing dan tiga rakyat Malaysia, termasuk seorang lelaki dipercayai pemilik resort berkenaan, lapor Utusan Malaysia.
Warga asing yang ditahan terdiri daripada 88 warga China, dua warga Myanmar, serta masing-masing seorang dari Indonesia, Hong Kong, Vietnam, Kemboja dan Rusia, berusia antara 20 hingga 75 tahun.
Tiga rakyat Malaysia pula terdiri daripada individu disyaki pemilik resort serta seorang lelaki dan wanita yang dipercayai bekerja di premis berkenaan.

Antara barangan dirampas ialah 100 telefon bimbit, 120 komputer, sistem CCTV, sembilan pek kad SIM belum digunakan, wang tunai RM5,000 serta 11 set Starlink yang dipercayai digunakan untuk mendapatkan akses internet.
Pegawai turut merampas 49 pasport China, masing-masing satu pasport Myanmar, Kemboja, Indonesia, Hong Kong dan Rusia, selain satu dokumen perjalanan Indonesia.
Zakaria berkata sindiket itu dipercayai menyewa premis resort berkenaan pada kadar kira-kira RM30,000 sebulan.

Menurutnya, lokasi resort yang agak terpencil memudahkan kegiatan itu dijalankan, selain sindiket dipercayai menggunakan individu tertentu sebagai pemerhati bagi memantau pergerakan keluar masuk kawasan terbabit.
Bercakap pada sidang media hari ini, Zakaria berkata siasatan awal mendapati sindiket itu dipercayai berpindah dari satu negara ke negara lain bagi mengelak dikesan pihak berkuasa.
Rekod dalam pasport yang dirampas menunjukkan anggota sindiket terbabit sebelum ini pernah beroperasi di Kemboja dan Vietnam.
Zakaria berkata sindiket itu dipercayai menggunakan Starlink kerana sistem berkenaan menggunakan sambungan satelit dan tidak bergantung kepada rangkaian telekomunikasi tempatan.

Katanya, 48 tahanan disiasat mengikut Seksyen 6(1)(c) Akta Imigresen 1959/63, manakala 45 lagi disiasat mengikut Seksyen 15(1)(c) akta sama dan dua individu di bawah Peraturan 39(b) Peraturan-Peraturan Imigresen 1963.
Tiga rakyat Malaysia pula ditahan mengikut Seksyen 56(1)(d) Akta Imigresen.
fa4c4770d5a89534: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — An alarming claim that an 11-year-old girl had left her school with a man on a motorcycle was fabricated by a fellow pupil after a dispute between the pair, police have said.

Kulim district police chief Superintendent Syamsul Sinring said investigations found the girl had never left the school grounds and had instead hidden inside a toilet after an argument with a friend, Utusan Malaysia reported.
Police were alerted after the school’s Senior Assistant for Student Affairs received information from two female pupils claiming the girl had left the premises with a man on a motorcycle.
But investigators later established that the account was false.
“Investigations found that the pupil arrived at school as usual at 7.20am after being dropped off by her older sister and attended the school assembly at about 8am,” Syamsul said.
“During the assembly, the pupil was believed to have played with her friend’s hair bun before the friend pulled her headscarf, causing her inner scarf to come off.”
Syamsul said the 11-year-old then went to the toilet to fix her headscarf, but remained there instead of returning to class.
While she was missing from the classroom, one of her friends told the school’s Senior Assistant for Student Affairs that the girl had left the school grounds with a man on a motorcycle.
“However, during questioning, her friend admitted that she had made up the story because she was upset with the pupil,” Syamsul said.
“Another pupil who knew that the story was untrue also went along with the claim.”
Police subsequently confirmed that the girl had remained inside the school throughout the episode and had not been taken away by any man.
The incident had initially sparked concern at the school before investigators pieced together what had happened.
e97caddcc741515a: TASEK GELUGOR: A 35-year-old motorcyclist was seriously injured after his motorcycle collided with a lorry in Kubang Menerong yesterday.
Seberang Prai Utara district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Abdul Rahman said the accident occurred at about 11am.
He said the crash involved a Mitsubishi rigid cargo lorry and a Honda motorcycle.

"Initial investigations found that the lorry was travelling along the left lane of the straight road towards Bukit Mertajam when the motorcyclist, who was travelling ahead, attempted to pass the lorry from its left side in the wrong direction.
"This resulted in the motorcycle colliding with the front left side of the lorry," he said.
Anuar said the motorcyclist was seriously injured and was taken to the emergency unit at Seberang Jaya Hospital for further treatment.
The case is being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Video footage of the incident has since gone viral.
763b843532f014a1: SINGAPORE, Oct 6 — The Singapore government will soon table legislation to reinforce a deterrence-based sentencing approach for scam offenders and those who facilitate scams, including young offenders, Senior Minister K. Shanmugam said today.

CNA reported that the proposed law comes in response to a High Court ruling in September that imposed probation and community-based sentences on several young money mule offenders, placing greater emphasis on rehabilitation rather than deterrence.

Speaking in Parliament, Shanmugam said the court’s reasoning was inconsistent with established sentencing guidelines, which recommend imprisonment or reformative training for scam-related offences because of the need to deter such crimes and protect the public.
“This is not the time to go soft,” said Shanmugam, who is also Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs.
He said the government’s position is that offenders involved in scams, regardless of age, must be dealt with firmly to discourage others from participating in such schemes.

“If a number of cases are dealt with seriously, many would-be offenders would take reference,” he said, adding that stronger deterrence would make it harder for scam syndicates to recruit accomplices and reduce the number of victims.

The issue arose after a three-judge High Court panel heard an appeal involving Mohamed Erzan Taib Zohri and six related scam cases. The seven cases involved money mule offenders, six of whom were below the age of 21. The court allowed appeals in four cases and imposed probation and community-based sentences.

Shanmugam noted that while rehabilitation remains an important principle in Singapore’s justice system, scam offences have significant social and financial consequences that require a different approach.
He pointed to the impact on victims, particularly elderly Singaporeans. In 2025 alone, more than 5,000 senior citizens fell victim to scams, losing around S$200 million collectively.
“Who is responsible? The scammers. Who helped them? The person who gave off his or her bank account, including young persons who do it to earn a few hundred dollars,” he said.
The minister warned that treating young offenders more leniently could encourage criminal syndicates to target and recruit youths as money mules.
“We cannot allow this to happen,” he said.

According to Shanmugam, the Ministry of Home Affairs will introduce legislation “soon” to clearly establish Parliament’s policy position and make explicit that the sentencing approach adopted in the Erzan case should not become the norm.
Scams remain Singapore’s most common crime category, with police receiving an average of 90 reports daily involving about S$2 million in losses each day.

The government is particularly concerned about youth involvement in scam-related offences. More than 1,000 youths were investigated in connection with scam reports in 2025, many of whom acted as money mules by handing over bank accounts, Singpass credentials, SIM cards or telephone lines to criminal syndicates.
Shanmugam said many young offenders were attracted by promises of quick money and were fully aware that their actions were unlawful.
“They knew that they shouldn’t be doing it, but they were tempted by the S$800, S$1,000 that they were offered,” he said.

While reaffirming the government’s commitment to rehabilitation and education for young offenders, Shanmugam said these objectives must be balanced against the need to prevent scams and protect potential victims.

He added that the authorities will continue to work with schools and parents on anti-scam education, while exploring structured scam-awareness and financial-literacy programmes for youths who come into contact with the law.
629d954665bdca2d: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) will be given access to the control room overseeing more than 5,000 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said discussions had been initiated with Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) to allow MCBA to access the control room and monitor the CCTV system for security purposes.
He said the cameras at KLIA Terminals 1 and 2 were currently managed by MAHB, which operated its own control room.

"Because MCBA is the new agency responsible for border control, discussions have already begun with MAHB to give MCBA access to the control room, which receives feeds from more than 5,000 CCTV cameras, so that the system can be monitored and managed not only by MAHB but also by MCBA," he said in the Dewan Rakyat.

He was responding to Afnan Hamimi Taib Azamudden (PN-Alor Star) who asked about the circulation of a viral video showing MCBA director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain berating two men, with one of them appearing to be grabbed forcefully by the ears
Saifuddin said the arrangement had been agreed upon and was currently at the administrative stage before it could be implemented.
He said MCBA would also install additional CCTV cameras in the second phase of the security measures, particularly at identified blind spots.
Saifuddin said the existing Immigration control room was focused on monitoring entry and exit counters, while MAHB's more comprehensive CCTV system covered the wider airport environment.
He said MAHB's primary interest was passengers, meaning security considerations were not entirely under its control.
"Therefore, MCBA will look at it from a security perspective," he said.
8dff901db7bfc683: BUCHAREST: Romania's centrist President Nicusor Dan nominated diplomat Luca Niculescu as prime minister late on Monday in another attempt to end a protracted political crisis that has raised debt costs and pressured the country's investment-grade rating.

"I chose the person with the highest chances of reaching a (parliamentary majority) and (he) has the freedom to decide the governing formula — political, technocrat — after talks he will hold with political parties," Dan said on Monday evening.
"I have the guarantee that a government with Luca Niculescu will maintain Romania's pro-Western direction and will respect the financial targets and all the commitments that Romania has undertaken."
Niculescu, 55, a former journalist and later Romanian ambassador to France, is currently interim deputy foreign minister, in charge of Romania's ongoing accession process to the OECD.
He is Dan's fourth attempt at nominating a prime minister in the five months since a pro-European broad coalition government collapsed in a no-confidence vote.
Niculescu now has 10 days to put together a cabinet list and ask parliament for a vote of confidence.

A previous pro-European government led by Liberal Party head Ilie Bolojan collapsed in early May when the leftist Social Democrats, parliament's biggest party, quit and teamed up with the far-right opposition to file a no-confidence vote.
It was unclear whether the pro-European parties in the now collapsed coalition would agree to back Niculescu's pending cabinet.
Under Romanian law, conditions for the president to dissolve parliament and call a snap election have been met, but Dan has repeatedly said that would be his last resort.

Analysts have said the only party to benefit from snap polls would be the opposition hard-right Alliance for Uniting Romanians (AUR), which leads opinion polls by double digits. Dan has also said any new government should not include AUR.

All three main ratings agencies have kept Romania on the last rung of investment-grade with a negative outlook in their scheduled reviews this year and have stressed the country needs to pass a 2027 budget by the end of this year, laying out further reductions to the deficit.
aae75dacb46f058b: SEPANG: Cadillac Formula 1 (F1) driver Valtteri Bottas has swapped four wheels for two, cycling 350km from Sepang to Singapore ahead of this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix.
The 37-year-old Finn began the journey just hours after Sunday's race at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), taking gravel roads, dirt tracks and palm oil plantation routes as he headed south.
"Yes, I am cycling to Singapore via roads less travelled," he said in an Instagram post.
The journey is expected to take several days, with Bottas due to join the F1 paddock for the Singapore Grand Prix from Oct 9 to 11.
Records shared on his Strava account, a fitness-tracking platform that tracks activities such as cycling routes, distance and duration, showed that his first stop was Port Dickson.
Bottas covered 56.6km in just over two hours before continuing south, completing another 161.91km in more than five hours to reach Muar, Johor.
The cycling trip comes after Bottas' disappointment at the Bahrain Grand Prix, where he retired on lap nine after going off the track into a gravel area.

It also gives the cycling enthusiast a chance to pursue his passion for gravel riding after he missed the 2026 Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) Gravel World Championships in Australia due to a scheduling clash with the Singapore Grand Prix.
Bottas was accompanied on the journey by his partner, Australian professional cyclist Tiffany Cromwell.
He is expected to complete the ride to Singapore ahead of Friday's opening practice session.

7d4a96cb8ea4c667: KUALA LUMPUR: Top Glove Corp Bhd's earnings more than doubled in the financial year ended Aug 31, 2026 (FY26) supported by growth in global demand.
Its net profit surged to RM307.96 million from RM105.33 million in FY25 as an improved demand-supply balance allowed manufacturers to rebuild margins after several challenging years.
Revenue for the financial year climbed 21.1 per cent year-on-year to RM4.23 billion from RM3.49 billion last year.
The group said the ongoing Middle East crisis further tightened raw material and glove supply, supporting cost pass-through and contributing to further margin improvement.
"Top Glove's continual quality and cost optimisation initiatives significantly reinforced its global competitive edge.
"The group's strengthened position enabled competitive pricing, driving strong sales volume growth and higher capacity utilisation.
"This was additionally supported by ongoing process automation, which helped mitigate industrywide manpower constraints," Top Glove said in a statement.
Top Glove's net cash position improved to RM141 million in FY26, versus a new debt position of RM267 million in FY25, reflecting a healthier financial structure and increased operational flexibility.
For the quarter ended Aug 31, 2025 (Q4 FY26), its net profit rose more than threefold to RM157.63 million from RM34.83 million. Revenue rose to RM1.25 billion from 893.56 million.

Top Glove joint managing directors Ng Yong Lin and Lim Jin Feng said FY26 marked another milestone for the group as it more than doubled its profitability compared to last year despite ongoing industry headwinds.

"This is testament to our global competitiveness, which is the result of the disciplined execution of ongoing improvements in quality and cost efficiency, and strong customer relationships across key international markets.
"We remain highly appreciative of our people for their higher productivity and good efforts, which have been instrumental in sustaining our upward trajectory," they added.
The company announced a tax exempt final dividend of 1.5 sen per share for FY26, payable on Dec 15.
This represents a 213 per cent increase in dividend per share compared with FY25.
The total dividend outlay for FY26 amounts to RM120 million, three times FY25's payout.
Top Glove said the industry outlook remains promising, anchored by steady demand growth for gloves, which remain essential items across the healthcare, industrial and food and beverage sectors.

While challenges including cost increases, raw material supply and price volatility, competition and manpower shortages persist, the group is confident of mitigating these headwinds through continuous quality enhancement and cost optimisation measures.

Top Glove is implementing cost saving measures which include heat energy efficiency partnerships with vendors, as well as expanding artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced automation across operations
This safeguards margins and maintains cost leadership to manage upcoming cost pressures, particularly the scheduled increase in natural gas tariffs effective Oct 1.
"The continued demand for gloves provides a solid foundation for long-term growth," said executive chairman Tan Sri Lim Wee Chai.

"While market conditions remain dynamic, the group's strong focus on working hard, smart and fast, coupled with improvements in quality and cost efficiency, people productivity and AI integration, will ensure we remain competitive and well-equipped to navigate industry challenges," he added.

44ad33b86731dc77: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Malaysia’s economy is expected to grow by 5.1 per cent this year and 4.7 per cent in 2027, largely driven by external demand from artificial intelligence (AI)-related investment and exports, according to the World Bank.
Lead economist for Malaysia Apurva Sanghi said the revision is 0.7 per cent percentage points higher from its previous April forecast and above regional growth of 4.5 per cent.

“Malaysia has recorded the strongest AI-driven export growth in the region, with more than 70 per cent of the country’s overall export growth in early 2026 attributed to increased demand for AI related products.

“So, Malaysia is really riding the AI wave, and while it sounds good, the corollary is that growth excluding AI-related goods has been weak, raising concerns about the economy’s dependence on the AI sector. A slowdown in global AI investment could significantly impact on Malaysia,” he said during a media briefing on October 2026 East Asia and Pacific (EAP) Economic Update today.

He cautioned that a potential reversal in the global AI boom is a key downside risk to Malaysia’s economic outlook, adding that fully realising the technology’s potential would require faster adoption and broader diffusion.
“Malaysia still lags in equipping its population with strong foundational skills, as highlighted in previous Malaysia Economic Monitor reports and other studies,” he said.

Apurva said a sharp reversal could affect Malaysia through two channels: financial channels, wherein the repricing of AI assets could trigger capital outflows from emerging markets, and the real economy channels, through a slowdown in global trade, especially given Malaysia’s strong linkages to the US and China.
“A repricing of AI related assets could prompt global risk aversion and tighten financial conditions, potentially leading to capital outflows from emerging markets including Malaysia.

“The second channel is through the real economy particularly slowdown in trade. If the US growth slows, that has an impact on Malaysia’s growth. In fact, in previous analysis, we showed that a one-percentage-point slowdown in the US growth lowers Malaysia’s growth by 0.8 percentage point,” he said.

Meanwhile, chief economist for Asia Franziska Ohnsorge said the EAP region’s growth is projected to moderate to 4.5 per cent in 2026-2027 or 0.3 percentage point higher than the projected six months ago. This is largely driven by strong high tech investment and exports in countries that are part of the AI value chain.
Several countries in the region, including China, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam are benefitting significantly from their roles in value chains for goods related to AI.
“But elsewhere in the region, high energy prices are weighing on growth prospects. The influence of AI on the region’s industry is unmistakable.

“AI is already reshaping labour demand, with firms increasingly seeking workers with both AI-related and complementary skills, particularly in areas such as mathematics, communications and collaboration,” she said.
Ohnsorge said East Asia’s electronics sector is a major participant in AI-related value chains and that is helping support growth even while cost of the energy is holding back other sectors.
She said AI-related products account for more than half of export growth in several East Asian countries and more than 70 per cent of export growth in Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.

At the same time, she said elevated energy prices continue to weigh on growth prospects and have contributed to higher inflation across the region in 2026, with price pressures expected to remain elevated into 2027.

Looking ahead, she noted that the downside risks to the growth outlook include a potential slowdown in global AI-related activity, persistently high energy prices and greater-than-expected damage from El Nino, particularly through its impact on agricultural production. — Bernama
4dcb9b3e73d7857e: The country’s 85-medal haul included athletes who trained with limited money and borrowed equipment. Plus, the Mumbai performer turning everyday absurdities into comedy In a country where cricket eclipses every other sport, the recently concluded Asian Games offered a much-needed reminder of India’s breadth of sporting talent. In this edition of the games, in Japan, India won 85 medals: 21 golds, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals. I admit I did not know many of the players competing, or even some of the sports they play before putting this piece together. Learning about the stories, I wonder why not. There were individual breakthroughs, records broken and history made. There were also hard-fought team victories, including the Indian women’s hockey team gold medal after a 44-year wait. Continue reading...
8ebd097b90b3eee0: OCTOBER 6 — Whenever adults hear the words “digital games”, the conversation almost immediately turns to screen time. How many hours are children spending online? Should phones be banned? Are games distracting them from learning?
Perhaps we are asking the wrong question. Instead of focusing only on how long young people spend in front of screens, we should also ask “What are they doing with those screens?”

There is a significant difference between consuming technology and creating with it. A recent Universiti Utara Malaysia initiative involving 88 lower-secondary students and teacher mentors from three schools demonstrated what can happen when students are challenged not merely to play digital games, but to design them.

Creating a game requires students to make decisions about rules, scoring, characters, logic, user experience and technical problems. Mathematics emerges through calculations and game systems. Technology becomes a tool for creation. Engineering thinking appears when students test an idea, encounter failure, make adjustments and try again.
The author argues that digital games can become powerful STEM learning tools when children move beyond consuming technology to designing, experimenting and creating with it. — File pic

STEM, therefore, stops being something students simply read about. It becomes something they build. Students were also introduced to artificial intelligence when developing 3D characters. This offers another important lesson. AI literacy should never mean pressing a button and accepting whatever the machine produces. Young people need to learn how to use AI while retaining human judgement, creativity, originality, ethics and responsibility.

Their digital games were eventually showcased through a metaverse exhibition, giving students an authentic audience for their creations. Learning changes when students know that what they produce will be seen, tested and discussed by others. Of course, digital games are no cure-all for declining STEM interest, and not every lesson needs gamification. If Malaysia wants a generation that is digitally fluent, telling children simply to “put down the screen” is no longer enough.
We should be teaching them to do something more powerful with it. Perhaps the future of STEM begins when a child stops asking, “What game can I play?” and starts asking, “What can I build?”
* Hapini Awang is a Research Fellow at the Institute for Advanced and Smart Digital Opportunities (IASDO) of the School of Computing at Universiti Utara Malaysia.
** This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
c36c3d344ea7edfe: KUALA LUMPUR: Memperkukuh sistem perlindungan sosial Malaysia harus kekal sebagai keutamaan dalam Belanjawan 2027, termasuk meningkatkan kecukupan manfaat, meluaskan liputan kepada pekerja ekonomi gig dan mempertingkat sokongan untuk golongan warga emas, menurut Bank Dunia.

Ketua Ahli Ekonomi untuk Malaysia, Apurva Sanghi, berkata kerajaan telah melakukan tugas dengan baik dalam memperluas dan meningkatkan skala program bantuan sosial, tetapi masih wujudnya jurang dari segi kecukupan manfaat berkenaan.
“Syabas kepada kerajaan kerana memperluas dan meningkatkan skala program bantuan sosial sehingga berjaya dengan cemerlang. Tetapi terdapat isu dari segi kecukupan, iaitu terhadap manfaat sedia ada.

“Saya fikir pekerja ekonomi gig masih tidak dilindungi di bawah perlindungan pengangguran dan sistem insurans pekerjaan,” katanya kepada taklimat media mengenai Laporan Kemas Kini Ekonomi Asia Timur dan Pasifik Bank Dunia bagi Oktober 2026 hari ini.
Beliau berkata, peluasan perlindungan untuk merangkumi pekerja ekonomi gig boleh dipertimbangkan, mungkin dengan beberapa bentuk mekanisme padanan tertentu daripada kerajaan.
Selain itu, Apurva berkata Malaysia merupakan sebuah negara yang semakin menua dengan pesat, tetapi perlindungan sosial masih belum mencakupi golongan warga emas dengan secukupnya.

Katanya, ramai warga emas tidak menerima sokongan yang mencukupi, sambil menyatakan skim pencen sosial tanpa caruman ketika ini hanya meliputi kira-kira empat peratus daripada golongan berusia 60 tahun ke atas.
“Jadi, usaha memperluas dan meningkatkan skala perlindungan sosial untuk golongan warga emas adalah sesuatu yang wajar dilaksanakan,” katanya.
Bagaimanapun, beliau menegaskan ini adalah cadangan yang dikemukakan semasa taklimat itu dan tidak semestinya akan diterima atau dimasukkan ke dalam belanjawan berkenaan.
a786c5cd3a24a6d8: PETALING JAYA: Ninety-eight people were arrested in a raid on a resort in Sungai Lembing, Pahang, which had been closed since last year but was allegedly being used as a base for an international scam syndicate.
Immigration director-general Zakaria Shaaban said 95 foreigners and three Malaysians were held, including a man believed to be the resort owner, Utusan Malaysia reported.
The foreigners comprised 88 Chinese nationals, two Myanmar nationals, and one each from Indonesia, Hong Kong, Vietnam, Cambodia and Russia, aged between 20 and 75.
The three Malaysians comprised the suspected resort owner and a man and woman believed to work there.
Seized items included 100 mobile phones, 120 computers, a CCTV system, nine packs of unused SIM cards, RM5,000 in cash and 11 Starlink sets believed to have been used for internet access.
Officers also took 49 Chinese passports, one passport each from Myanmar, Cambodia, Indonesia, Hong Kong and Russia, and an Indonesian travel document.
Zakaria said the syndicate was believed to have rented the resort premises for about RM30,000 a month.
"Its location was rather remote, and the syndicate also used certain individuals as lookouts to monitor movements in and out of the area," he was quoted as saying at a press conference today.

Zakaria said preliminary investigations suggested that the syndicate moved between countries to avoid detection, with records in the seized passports showing that its members previously operated in Cambodia and Vietnam.
He said the syndicate likely used Starlink because it relies on satellites, not local telecommunications networks.

Zakaria said 48 detainees were being investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, while 45 were being investigated under Section 15(1)(c) of the same Act, and two under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.
The three Malaysians are being held under Section 56(1)(d).
cc13737f3ee64d67: PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department will work with other enforcement agencies to tackle foreigners suspected of operating businesses using licences belonging to locals under so-called "Ali Baba" arrangements.

Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said matters involving business licences did not fall under the department's jurisdiction, but it would assist other agencies in joint enforcement operations where immigration offences were involved.
"Licences and related matters are outside of the department's jurisdiction. There are other agencies responsible for enforcing this.

"However, we will cooperate with other agencies to assist in carrying out operations, particularly to combat activities which violate immigration regulations or the Immigration Act," he told reporters in a press conference.
Zakaria urged members of the public with information on foreigners suspected of being involved in such activities to lodge complaints with the department.
Zakaria was responding to questions over videos circulating on social media purportedly highlighting the continued use of "Ali Baba" business arrangements in Kuala Lumpur.
One such video shows a man confronting people at several business premises and questioning them over who owned the businesses and the licences under which they were operating.
Text accompanying the video claims that business licences belonging to locals were being used by foreigners, including those from China and India, to operate businesses.
b01ebb5e6b789633: BEIJING: Coco Gauff said she had received an "insane" amount of racial abuse on social media after the two-time Grand Slam champion beat local teenager Sun Xinran at the China Open on Monday in a match where a replayed point sparked an online backlash.

The American won 7-5 6-1 to reach the fourth round, but was targeted after stopping play during a crucial point in the first set, raising her hand to complain about a flickering advertising board just as Sun was about to put away a winner.
After a video review, the umpire ordered the point to be replayed. Gauff won the replayed point and held serve for 5-5 before cruising to victory against the Chinese 16-year-old.
Gauff, 22, said she had received a barrage of abusive messages on social media after the match.
"You can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist," Gauff, who is Black, said on X early on Tuesday in reply to a post containing a racial slur.
"The amount of racist comments/direct messages I've received in the last few hours is insane.
"Lastly, I'm not a cheater or a thief," she said
Reuters has contacted the WTA, the governing body of women's tennis, and tournament organisers in Beijing for comment.
The WTA has made efforts to tackle the issue of online abuse by introducing an AI-powered system which monitors thousands of players and officials on social media.
A study by the WTA and World Tennis showed players were subjected to over 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media in 2025, up from 8,000 posts a year earlier.
Gauff also explained that she was following the rules when she challenged the point.
Players are allowed to request video reviews of select judgment calls, including claims a distraction may have interfered with play.
The American said she had spoken to Sun about the point at the end of the match.
"Xinran's an incredible talent and player, I apologised for the situation at the end of the match and she completely understood," she wrote.

"I didn't like to see her so emotional as I've been there and I really understand what it's like, but this is the beginning of an incredible career. It was an honour to share the court in front of her home crowd," she said.
c21ac954d95ab14d: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 6 — The Penang government will strengthen coordination with Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) to plan the expansion of international air connectivity in tandem with the ongoing expansion of Penang International Airport (PIA).

State Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said early planning was crucial to ensure PIA’s additional capacity could be fully utilised once the expansion project is completed within the next two years.

He said the project would increase PIA’s annual passenger capacity from the current 6.8 million to 12 million, creating opportunities to introduce new international routes and increase flight frequencies on existing routes.

“The next priority will be to fully utilise this additional capacity by opening new routes and increasing flight frequencies on existing routes; therefore, it is crucial that we make early preparations at this stage and work closely with MAHB to put the necessary plans in place,” he said in a statement today.
Wong said he recently met MAHB senior officials in Kuala Lumpur to discuss the expansion and upgrading of PIA, as well as the development of new air routes.

He said the Penang government had intensified efforts in recent years to develop direct air links between Penang and major international cities, which had helped boost tourist arrivals while generating wider tourism and economic benefits.
Wong said the Penang government and MAHB would hold regular meetings on route development, aviation market trends and future projects involving PIA.

He also urged MAHB to continue giving attention to PIA’s position as Malaysia’s second busiest airport and further harness its potential as an aviation hub, including through timely sharing of aviation market intelligence and relevant data.
Wong said air cargo also had significant growth potential, given Penang’s concentration of multinational corporations and their increasing demand for international logistics and air freight services.

He said the Penang government had urged the federal government to strengthen the tourism development agenda under Budget 2027, including through an International Air Connectivity Fund with matching grants to attract more direct flights from strategic markets such as Japan, South Korea, Australia and the Middle East. — Bernama
ab93e3ccb41df273: PETALING JAYA: A 19-year-old student believed to have been strangled by her boyfriend following an argument was found dead at a house in Air Putih, Kuantan, early this morning.
Kuantan police chief Ashari Abu Samah said the boyfriend, also 19, was arrested at the scene after contacting the police himself at 4.32am to report the incident, according to Berita Harian.
"The victim was found lying unconscious on a bed. We found strangulation marks on her," he was quoted as saying.
He said preliminary investigations suggested that the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding between the two.
A post-mortem will be conducted at Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital to determine the cause of death.
Police are recording statements from witnesses and have urged those with information regarding the incident to step forward.
The suspect has been remanded for seven days until Oct 12 for investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
f618c288e6cc270c: KUALA LUMPUR: Crime prevention specialist Shamir Rajadurai today urged institutions to stop focusing solely on the latest scam tactics and instead understand how criminals think.

Speaking at a media roundtable in conjunction with a conference here, Shamir said institutions should study criminals' thought processes in the same way that businesses study their customers when developing products.
He said this would allow institutions to identify weaknesses in their systems and anticipate how criminals might exploit them.
"The biggest problem is that we are always focusing on the tactic. We’re like, okay, what’s happening now? What’s happening next? We don’t focus on the criminal, and that’s the biggest problem.

"Everyone is only focusing on the data that they’ve received. They’re not looking back and thinking, no, I need to start thinking like a criminal," he said at the Intelligence-Led Financial Crime Prevention: The Power of Data, Insights and Collaboration conference.

Citing his experience in demonstrating how seemingly sophisticated locks can be bypassed using simple methods, Shamir said the same approach should be applied to financial crime prevention, where compliance officers should ask how criminals can circumvent existing controls.
He gave the example of mule accounts, saying criminals know that banks cannot simply profile every customer entering the system.
"If I’m a criminal, I understand that’s my loophole. As a bank, you need to figure out how to close that loophole," he said.

Meanwhile, Transparency International Malaysia president Raymon Ram said the organisation was interviewing convicted mule-account offenders in prisons to better understand how they were recruited and why they became involved.
Raymon said the research focused on understanding how people were recruited, why they agreed to participate and whether they understood the consequences of becoming a mule.
"Not all mules know that they are mules," he added.

Giving the example of university students, he said they could be approached through what appeared to be legitimate job opportunities, and asked to open bank accounts or allow their accounts to be used for online bank transfers.
"They think that it’s a job opportunity for students," he said.
bdee51633ac2d650: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 259 Malaysian trainees have completed specialised railway training in China and will form the pioneer workforce operating and maintaining the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL).
The trainees will take on various roles, according to Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak.
This includes station operations, electric multiple-unit (EMU) maintenance, signalling, assistant train driving and locomotive driving.
The 259 were selected in three batches in 2025 to undergo a one-year BNKI training programme at the Yuzhou Railway Occupational Medical College/LRBTC in Yuzhou, China.

The programme is designed to give the trainees practical exposure to railway operations and maintenance, preparing them to form part of ECRL's pioneer operating workforce once the line begins commercial operations.

The training is part of a longer-term workforce development effort under Industrial Skills Training Programme, or PLKI, which was launched in June 2017, aimed at building the technical skills and operational expertise needed to support ECRL over the long term.
Meanwhile, Darwis said the ECRL's wider impact would ultimately depend on how businesses, communities and industries use the new connectivity.
"It gives Malaysia a new way to travel between the East Coast and the Klang Valley and gives businesses a new way to move goods," he said.
MRL is also studying a proposed extension from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang, which could strengthen passenger connectivity with southern Thailand and create longer-term freight opportunities.
The proposal has gained momentum, with Malaysia and China agreeing to the proposed extension, although further discussions with stakeholders are required before it is brought to the Cabinet.
The proposed link will connect with the existing Pasir Mas-Rantau Panjang railway, which has been inactive for years.
The government is also looking at how the existing Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd line could be integrated with the ECRL to optimise costs and connectivity.
Darwis said such connectivity could eventually strengthen Malaysia-Thailand rail links and provide another channel for regional trade.
dcac824da825692b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Malaysia will harness its chairmanship and role as host of the 28th Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee (MSC) meeting next year to strengthen Asean solidarity and shared responsibility in tackling transboundary haze.

Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the platform would provide an important avenue for strengthening regional cooperation to prevent a recurrence of haze incidents.
“Our approach is clear. Transboundary haze must be addressed through collective action and stronger regional cooperation, rather than pointing fingers or assigning blame to any party.

“More importantly, each member state must fulfil its respective responsibilities and work together to strengthen prevention measures, preparedness and early action,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

He said this in response to a supplementary question from Datuk Yusuf Abd Wahab (GPS-Tanjong Manis) on Malaysia’s plans to propose new initiatives at the Asean level to address the transboundary haze problem more effectively and sustainably.
Arthur said the efforts included enhancing data and information sharing, strengthening the implementation of domestic laws, and stepping up enforcement cooperation among Asean member states.
He said the approach would be crucial in turning commitments under the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP) into tangible, consistent and effective action on the ground.

Arthur said Malaysia had also tabled proposals on “Science Diplomacy” and a “Sustainable Haze Fund” at the 27th Sub-Regional MSC Meeting on Transboundary Haze Pollution in Bali, Indonesia, last July, with both proposals now under review by the Asean Secretariat.
“Science diplomacy aims to enhance the use of data, technology and scientific evidence in Asean policy development and decision-making on haze prevention, monitoring and management.
“The Sustainable Haze Fund, meanwhile, seeks to provide sustainable and reliable funding for regional fire prevention and haze management efforts,” he said.
Arthur said Malaysia would continue discussions on both proposals at the 21st Committee Meeting and the Conference of the Parties (COP) to the AATHP, scheduled to be held in Vietnam this December.

Responding to Yusuf’s question on measures to address transboundary haze, particularly in Sarawak, and the diplomatic or legal steps taken, Arthur said air quality monitoring and haze management in the state had been stepped up, including through Cloud Seeding Operations conducted from September 3 to 7.

On the diplomatic front, he said direct consultations were held with Indonesia’s Environment Minister via a telephone call on August 24 to expedite fire-fighting efforts in affected areas, alongside the submission of a formal letter to the Asean Secretariat.

Arthur said Malaysia also submitted a formal offer of assistance to Indonesia on September 9, covering aerial firefighting operations involving water bombing, amphibious aircraft support and cloud seeding.

He said the Indonesian government agreed to Malaysia’s offer of assistance on September 18 during a meeting between the Deputy Prime Minister and the President of Indonesia, with both countries now coordinating the deployment of aid through their respective Foreign Ministries. — Bernama
5aad3c89205053d3: KUALA LUMPUR: Social media personality and teacher Cikgu Zack Kirana has expressed frustration with parents who allegedly place the responsibility of shaping their children's character entirely on teachers.
Zack said schools play an important role in providing education and instilling discipline, but a child's character and values must begin at home.
While teachers have a role in guiding students' behaviour and moral development, she insisted that the responsibility should not rest entirely on educators.
"Character development begins at home. The school is an institution that adds other values such as education, discipline and life skills," she said.

Zack went on to question parents when children display serious behavioural problems, saying: "If a child acts like a monster and lacks basic compassion, hold the parents accountable before pointing fingers at the teacher."
She acknowledged that teachers may be able to identify behavioural issues among their students, but their influence has limits.
"No matter how good teachers are at detecting their students' behaviour, their role is very limited. They are not the parents," she said.

Zack also urged parents not to take criminal cases or misconduct involving their children lightly, warning: "When an underage criminal escapes justice, their parents shouldn't get off scot-free. This generation is becoming increasingly out of control!"
She agreed that schools should improve security measures but maintained that a child's character remains a crucial factor.
"Yes, schools need better security, but a troubled child will harm someone else's kid anywhere—even in an alleyway behind a row of houses," she said.
def9563f6e0dbf21: KUALA LUMPUR: The East Coast Rail Link's (ECRL) commercial operations has been brought forward to mid-December, with Phase 1 construction now 98.16 per cent complete and operational preparations gathering pace.

Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) said the 525km first phase, linking Gombak to Kota Bharu through 16 stations across Selangor, Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan, is entering the final stages of testing and commissioning.

MRL chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak said the targeted December start followed a request from the Transport Ministry for services to begin during the year-end school holidays, bringing forward the earlier January 2027 timeline.
The focus was now shifting from building the railway to ensuring it could operate safely, reliably and efficiently, he added.
"The ECRL is now moving from a project to a service," Darwis said at an editorial briefing today.
However, he stressed that the compressed timeline would not compromise safety or technical standards.

The system is undergoing integration testing covering signalling, communications, traction power and the overhead catenary system, while preparations are also under way for ticketing, onboard services, maintenance and other operational requirements.

ECRL Operations Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Mohd Zaidi Sharif said operational readiness currently stood at about 70.5 per cent and was targeted to reach 80 per cent by the end of this month, allowing trial operations to begin.

The passenger service will initially comprise six services in each direction on weekdays, comprising two express and four transit services. An additional service in each direction is planned for weekends.
The express service will stop at four major stations - ITT Gombak, Kuantan, Kuala Terengganu and Kota Bharu - while the transit service will serve all 16 stations.
The six-car electric multiple-unit (EMU) trains can carry up to 425 passengers and are designed to operate at speeds of up to 160km per hour.
An express journey from Gombak to Kuantan is expected to take about one hour and 35 minutes, followed by another one hour and 25 minutes to Kuala Terengganu and about an hour to Kota Bharu.
Darwis said he had completed a full-length test run on Sept 25, travelling between Gombak and Kota Bharu in about three hours and 20 minutes without intermediate stops.
He said a commercial journey of around four hours was achievable once station stops and operational requirements were factored in.
The ECRL is also expected to introduce a new freight option for manufacturers and businesses along the East Coast.
Its electric locomotives can haul up to 3,500 tonnes, with freight services expected to operate mainly at night when passenger services are less intensive.

ECRL Operation said discussions with manufacturers, including major industrial players, showed demand for an alternative to road transport, particularly for moving large volumes of cargo over long distances to ports.

The operator is targeting rail freight costs to be competitive with, and ultimately lower than, road transport, although the final structure will depend on how rail services are integrated with haulage and other last-mile logistics.
e47735d3cc6d6f90: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan has accused Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia of deliberately trying to “cripple” the coalition ahead of the Melaka state election by lodging a complaint with the Registrar of Societies (RoS).

The allegation was made in an affidavit filed in support of PN’s application for judicial review of two RoS notices that have thrown uncertainty over the coalition’s status as it prepares for the state polls, Malaysiakini reported today.
Takiyuddin claimed Bersatu acted in bad faith when it complained to the RoS after being left out of a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16.
“I sincerely believe that Bersatu did not lodge the complaint to defend any rights it had as a component party of PN.

“I sincerely believe that Bersatu lodged the complaint with the intention of crippling PN — a coalition that the party was opposing in an election at the time,” he was quoted as saying in the affidavit.
The PAS secretary-general was referring to the forthcoming Melaka state election, for which the Election Commission has yet to announce the key dates.
According to Malaysiakini, Takiyuddin cited a series of events in the affidavit which he said supported his contention that Bersatu’s complaint had been made with an ulterior motive.
He said PN had previously raised questions over the validity of Bersatu’s own supreme council and had written to the party seeking clarification.
The latest allegation marks a further escalation in the increasingly public rift between Bersatu and the coalition it helped establish.

PN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said last week that Bersatu had not formally been expelled from PN, while confirming that the coalition’s activities had been suspended following eight complaints lodged with the RoS.

The relationship had already deteriorated before the regulatory dispute. In August, Takiyuddin confirmed that Bersatu would not be involved in PN’s negotiations with Barisan Nasional over the Melaka election, although Bersatu continued to maintain that it remained a legitimate PN component party.
The RoS issued notices to PN on September 22 and 23 following Bersatu’s complaint that it had not been invited to the coalition’s Supreme Council meeting despite remaining a member.
PN was given 30 days to show cause to the regulator.
Takiyuddin subsequently accused the RoS of acting in bad faith and applying political pressure, an allegation that has not been established by the court.

PN yesterday filed a judicial review application at the Kuala Lumpur High Court seeking to challenge the two RoS notices and clarify whether it can contest the Melaka election using its name and logo. It has asked for the matter to be heard urgently before the Election Commission determines the election timetable.
884e3454e0871f46: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 6 — The Sabah government has introduced a new Outcome-Based Integrity (OBI) approach as a formula to build a resilient and corruption-resistant administrative ecosystem.

Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said OBI would focus on three key areas: significantly reducing the risk of leakages and fundamental misconduct, improving the efficiency and transparency of public service delivery, and increasing public and investor confidence.

He said every governance, integrity and anti-corruption instrument under OBI must deliver tangible results, stressing that integrity was not merely rhetoric but a key pillar underpinning the success of the Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) Development Plan.

“OBI outcome measures will form part of the annual Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for all heads of departments and leaders of state-owned companies, while administrative performance will be measured by the reduction in leakage risks and service efficiency.”

Hajiji said this when opening the 2026 Integrity, Governance and Anti-Corruption Convention (KITA), themed “Integrity Driving Sabah Maju Jaya Governance”, at the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) today.
The chief minister said every ringgit of public funds spent must deliver maximum value for money and directly benefit the people without being lost through leakages.
He said poorly managed bureaucracy created fertile ground for corruption and wastage.
“Governance will no longer be reactive but based on the 3P formula - Proactive, Predictive and Preventive — by preventing problems before they occur based on actual risk assessments,” he noted.

He said the state government would also strengthen digitalisation, data analytics and behavioural insights, while institutionalising OBI in agency performance assessments, while at the same time expanding the role of Certified Integrity Officers (CeIOs) and strengthening Integrity Units to develop a new generation of leaders grounded in integrity.
“Integrity is the driving force that ensures every public fund and government policy delivers optimum returns and tangible benefits to the people without leakage or misconduct,” he said.

Hajiji said more than 2,500 participants from across Sabah were attending the two-day KITA 2026, reflecting a collective commitment to strengthening governance, integrity and anti-corruption practices.

Since KITA was introduced in 2023, he said 10 CeIOs have been appointed to head Integrity Units in state ministries, while the i-Adu mobile application, i-DIMSS and i-STANS systems have been developed.
Another 17 Sabah state agency officers have obtained the Certification in Professional Integrity Assurance and Management (CPIAM) from Universiti Sains Malaysia.

Hajiji said the Sabah Integrity and Governance Division (BIGoNS) under the State Secretary’s Office had also received the UNGGUL recognition under the Integrity and Governance Management System (SPINE) certification by the Malaysian Institute of Integrity (IIM). — Bernama
8bafd737a96533af: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Mental health treatment in the country has demonstrated positive results, with 76 per cent of psychiatric patients under the Ministry of Health (MOH) successfully rehabilitated and reintegrated into the workforce as of June.

Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said this achievement, realised through the Community Mental Health Centre (Mentari) vocational support programme, surpassed the ministry’s Key Performance Indicator (KPI) target of 60 per cent.
He noted that mental health treatment in the country focuses not merely on symptom reduction but emphasises functional rehabilitation to enable patients to live independently.

“Mental health treatment aims not only to alleviate symptoms but also to help patients resume their daily lives with their families and return to work. Through 39 Mentari centres nationwide, patients receive support such as rehabilitation, psychosocial assistance, and aid in returning to the workforce and achieving independence,” he said during the question-and-answer session in Dewan Rakyat today.

He said this in response to a question from Datuk Adnan Abu Hassan (BN-Kuala Pilah), who sought information on the indicators of treatment effectiveness at government facilities, the mechanisms for evaluating success, and the rate of patients returning for further treatment.

Dzulkefly added that the quality of MOH treatment is further evidenced by the psychiatric patient hospital readmission rate within a three-month period, which stood at 6.32 per cent well within the KPI target of keeping the rate below 25 per cent.

Meanwhile, responding to a supplementary question from Adnan regarding the potential use of cannabis extracts for mental health treatment, Dzulkefly said the Ministry of Health (MOH) is open to medical clinical research, provided it is backed by scientific evidence.

However, he emphasised that the MOH strongly rejects any approach to fully decriminalise the use of the substance, drawing lessons from the public health crisis previously experienced in Thailand. — Bernama
9b7ea2e215f3ab13: HONG KONG, Oct 6 — Nicholas Tse might have upheld his bad-boy image in his younger days, but his longtime manager Mani Fok said he is not the most troublesome artiste she has managed.

The 54-year-old, who is also a producer and Emperor Entertainment Group’s chief executive officer, hosted Hong Kong singers Joey Yung, Mike Tsang, Angela Hui as well as Kenny Kwan – all signed under the group – in the first episode of her Bilibili talk show Manifest, released on Sept 25.
They started the episode with a game of truth-or-dare, where Mani was asked to talk about the most troublesome artiste she has managed.
Joey, 46, said it was Nicholas, with Mani responding: “The person you mentioned is one of them, but there is always a ‘higher mountain’.”

6503531de0aecee1: PETALING JAYA: The World Bank has raised its 2026 growth forecast for Malaysia from 4.4% to 5.1%, but warns that the economy's reliance on artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments will leave it vulnerable if the global AI boom slows.
Apurva Sanghi, the lead economist for Malaysia, said more than 70% of the country's export growth in early 2026 came from increased demand for AI-related products, Bernama reported.

"Malaysia is really riding the AI wave, and while it sounds good, the corollary is that growth excluding AI-related goods has been weak, raising concerns about the economy's dependence on the AI sector.
"A slowdown in global AI investment could significantly impact Malaysia," he was quoted as saying during a media briefing on the bank's East Asia and Pacific Economic Update.

Apurva said a reversal in the global AI boom could affect Malaysia through two channels: financial markets, where a repricing of AI-related assets could trigger capital outflows from emerging markets, and the real economy, through weaker global trade.

"If the US growth slows, that has an impact on Malaysia's growth. In fact, in previous analysis, we showed that a one-percentage-point slowdown in US growth lowers Malaysia's growth by 0.8 percentage point," he said.
Franziska Ohnsorge, the bank's chief economist for Asia, said the region's growth was projected to moderate to 4.5% in 2026-2027, 0.3 percentage point higher than the forecast six months ago.
She credited high-tech investment and exports in countries that are part of the AI value chain, including China, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.
"But elsewhere in the region, high energy prices are weighing on growth prospects. The influence of AI on the region's industry is unmistakable.

"AI is already reshaping labour demand, with firms increasingly seeking workers with AI-related and complementary skills, particularly in areas such as mathematics, communications and collaboration," she said.
Ohnsorge said AI-related products account for more than half of export growth in several East Asian countries and more than 70% of export growth in Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.
She said elevated energy prices also continue to weigh on growth prospects and contributed to higher inflation across the region in 2026, with price pressures expected to remain elevated into 2027.
Looking ahead, she said the downside risks to the growth outlook include a potential slowdown in global AI-related activity, persistently high energy prices and greater-than-expected damage.
4319adb01862650c: OpenAI is now offering API customers the option to watermark the output of certain models in order to comply with the letter of Europe's AI Act. And within a few weeks, the biz plans to apply a form of digital watermarking – like it or not – to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text output in the European Union. But unlike rival Anthropic, it isn't applying its watermarking technique to content generated outside of Europe, though API customers can choose to have the marks applied to content made anywhere. Moreover, OpenAI is using technology that misses a fair number of instances of AI-generated text and can easily be tricked. The EU AI Act requires generative AI service providers to make model output identifiable in a way that's readable by machines. Anthropic was the first major AI company to announce its approach to AI Act compliance, which involves the application of Google's SynthID-Text algorithm. It's doing so globally. Microsoft and Meta have been working on similar technology for image-based AI because the EU is not the only market in which people have raised concerns about content provenance and the potential to use AI-generated content to produce misinformation. OpenAI already applies other content provenance signals to AI-generated images, audio, and video. In keeping with the letter of the AI Act, OpenAI is now offering a text watermarking approach called textGrain [PDF] that "adds an invisible statistical signal to the model’s word choices. Our detector looks for that signal to assess whether a passage contains an OpenAI watermark." Large language models predict word tokens one at a time from a probability distribution of potential words. By picking a different word to emit periodically – ideally a synonym – the resulting text deviates from the statistical pattern produced by an unbiased model. A watermark detector, which OpenAI is making available only to approved researchers and organizations, should flag that vocabulary divergence. That's the theory, but in practice results vary. The target error rate is one percent, but in short passages of 200 words, the detector may only flag 80 percent of the watermarks, compared to 95 percent in a 400-word passage. The results are also worse in texts that are functional, like passages about math or code, as substitutions are more likely to introduce errors. The textGrain paper does not address the likelihood that a statistically altered word choice might alter the meaning of a given passage. That's a possibility if the algorithm were to alter some salient fact or figure. Anthropic's approach, which also replaces certain output words though using a different algorithm, brings similar risks. In any event, OpenAI's watermark is easily defeated by word substitution. In tests on 400-token passages, swapping out 10 percent of the words with synonyms reduced watermark detection from 92 percent to 66 percent. And when replacing 25 percent of words, the watermark signal could only be detected in 17 percent of cases. Now witness the firepower of this barely adequate but compliant AI detector… ®
08af0bb3280e6ecb: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 — Malaysia’s inflation is among the lowest in the region, but rising upstream cost pressures could pose an inflation risk later this year, said the World Bank lead economist Apurva Sanghi.
He said producer price inflation had swung from negative territory in December 2023 and February 2024 to over 10 per cent in June and almost 11 per cent in August this year.

This had renewed upstream cost pressures, presenting a potential inflation risk later in the year, he told the media during a briefing on the October 2026 East Asia and Pacific Economic Update here today.
Nevertheless, the World Bank projected headline inflation to rise modestly to two per cent this year, with subsidies limiting the pass-through of inflation to households despite higher energy prices.

Apurva said Malaysia recorded a relatively low inflation rate of 1.9 per cent in August 2026, compared with its regional peers Thailand (2.5 per cent), Indonesia (3.2 per cent), Vietnam (4.9 per cent) and the Philippines (6.1 per cent).
He said lower-income households, defined as those earning less than RM3,000 a month, faced milder price pressures.
Inflation for these households averaged only 1.2 per cent in the first half of this year and remained below headline inflation every month during the period, he said.
He said income growth and transfers had also outpaced living costs to a greater extent for lower-income households than for higher-income households.
On economic growth, Apurva said Malaysia had exceeded expectations, with external demand playing a starring role while domestic demand played a supporting role.
Private consumption growth rose to 4.8 per cent in the second quarter (2Q) from 4.7 per cent in the 1Q, while private investment growth slowed to 4.3 per cent from 7.8 per cent, he said.
He said private investment as a share of gross domestic product remained below its pre-pandemic level, standing at 15.8 per cent last year compared with 16.9 per cent during the 2015-2019 period.
Taking a broader perspective, Apurva said consumer sentiment, business confidence and private investment were not clearly trending upwards.
Consumer sentiment was at its lowest since 2022, based on industry research, while business confidence was as low as during the pandemic, he added. — Bernama
5fb8497bddcd3289: TOKYO: The Japanese coast guard said on Tuesday a Chinese survey ship had left Tokyo's exclusive economic zone (EEZ) after being ordered repeatedly to stop research operations that Japan said were unauthorised.

The Chinese vessel Kexue was first seen on Sept 27 in waters around 70km north of Ishigaki island in Japan's southernmost prefecture of Okinawa, "intermittently extending wire-like objects into the sea from her side and stern", coast guard spokesman Masashi Asano told AFP.

The vessel eventually left on Friday after the coast guard sent "radio messages demanding the survey be halted, stating that scientific research in our maritime zone without... consent will not be tolerated", Asano said.
The number of unapproved surveys by Chinese ships in Japan's EEZ has already more than doubled compared to last year, he said.

The UN Convention on the Law of the Sea stipulates that scientific research in an EEZ - an area of up to 200 nautical miles (370km) offshore from a country's land - requires an agreement from the nation that holds exclusive rights to the exploration and use of natural resources.
Asano said the frequency of unapproved surveys in Japan's EEZ had "surged" since around the time Japan and the Philippines announced they would start maritime border negotiations.
There have been 14 cases so far this year, compared to six last year, and one or two cases in the three years prior, he said.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Ferdinand Marcos agreed on May 28 to start formal negotiations to "delimit the maritime boundary of the exclusive economic zone and the continental shelf between the two countries... in order to enhance legal certainty in the region", according to a joint statement.
Beijing claims most of the South China Sea, a vital global trade route, despite an international ruling that its assertion has no legal basis.
Its coast guard has clashed repeatedly with that of the Philippines, sparking fears of an armed conflict.

Separately, coast guard vessels from both Japan and China routinely engage in standoffs around the Tokyo-controlled Senkaku islands in the East China Sea, islands that Beijing claims and calls the Diaoyu.
Takaichi called China an "important neighbour" in a policy address on Monday and pledged to build a stable relationship between the rival nations.

Diplomatic relations between the Asian economic giants have been at rock bottom since Takaichi suggested in November that Tokyo might intervene in any attack on Taiwan, which Beijing claims as its territory.

d3f6848ccd7a21b6: TOKYO: Suzuki Motor unveiled its first fully electric kei car, fuelling competition in Japan’s most important vehicle segment.

Including federal subsidies, the “e SKY” model will cost around ¥1.6 million (US$10,120) when sales start in November, Suzuki said Tuesday. That’s cheaper than Nissan Motor's top-selling Sakura EV and BYD’s first kei car the Chinese company introduced in July.

Kei cars are affordable, ultra-compact vehicles that account for more than a third of automobile sales in Japan. The arrival of the e SKY adds to signs that the country is becoming a key battleground for electric versions of the tiny cars, with Nissan, Honda, Daihatsu and now Suzuki offering them. Together, the Japanese brands control about 80% of the market.

Suzuki targets around 1,000 monthly sales for the tiny EV, which has a battery range of 310km (193 miles) and a base price of ¥2.1 million. Federal subsidies can bring its sticker down by around half a million yen. BYD said in July that its Racco kei car, which offers a minimum range of 210km, will cost less than ¥2 million including subsidies.

In Japan, where EV uptake is far lower than in the US, Europe or China, Suzuki is betting that its first electric kei car can help lower the barrier for customers to make the switch from gasoline vehicles.

“We asked ourselves what kind of product would convince kei drivers to shift to an EV, and this is our answer,” the model’s chief engineer Tomoyuki Tsubata told reporters in Tokyo. “We’re hoping this will help them recognise that option.”
eea765b0c69f086b: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) menyasarkan pengumuman harga tiket bagi operasi komersial Laluan Rel Pantai Timur (ECRL) dibuat pada bulan ini dengan jualan tiket dibuka pada November.
Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif MRL, Darwis Abdul Razak, berkata pengumuman itu dijangka dibuat Kementerian Pengangkutan dengan jangkaan operasi komersial ECRL bermula pada pertengahan Disember 2026.
“Kita menjangkakan harga tiket yang dinamik dan mampu milik, iaitu lebih rendah berbanding harga kapal terbang dan sedikit tinggi daripada bas,” katanya.
Darwis berkata demikian pada Taklimat ECRL kepada Pengarang Berhubung Kesiapsiagaan Operasi ECRL bersama dengan media di sini hari ini.
Beliau berkata untuk fasa pertama ECRL, bilangan perjalanan pergi balik dari Isnin hingga Khamis adalah sebanyak 12 kali dan 14 kali dari Jumaat hingga Ahad.

Selain itu, Darwis berkata pihaknya berpuas hati dengan kemajuan Fasa 1 (Kota Bharu-Gombak) projek ECRL yang mencapai 98.16% setakat September lepas, serta yakin sasaran operasi pada pertengahan Disember ini dapat dicapai.

Beliau turut menekankan prestasi memberangsangkan Comprehensive Inspection Train (C.I.T.) ECRL baru-baru ini yang melengkapkan perjalanan tanpa henti dari Gombak ke Kota Bharu dalam tempoh tiga jam 19 minit meliputi jarak 519 kilometer pada kelajuan sehingga 160 km/j.
Pencapaian itu mengesahkan keupayaan ECRL untuk menyediakan perkhidmatan ekspres di laluan Gombak-KotaSAS-Kuala Terengganu-Kota Bharu dalam tempoh kurang daripada empat jam.
Rangkaian ECRL sepanjang 665 kilometer merentas negeri Pantai Timur, iaitu Kelantan, Terengganu dan Pahang sebelum menghubungkan Selangor di pantai barat Semenanjung Malaysia.
ECRL dijangka memendekkan masa perjalanan antara Kota Bharu dan Gombak kepada kira-kira empat jam berbanding sekitar tujuh jam melalui pengangkutan jalan raya.
d3f77f3c25a18eb4: KUALA LUMPUR: Penjenayah semakin menggunakan kecerdasan buatan (AI) untuk mengautomasikan penipuan, mengenal pasti kelemahan dan memperhebat serangan siber, sekali gus menyukarkan jenayah kewangan dikesan, kata Gabenor Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour.
Rasheed berkata kira-kira 95% kes penipuan dalam talian melibatkan mangsa yang diperdaya sehingga memindahkan wang kepada penipu.
Katanya, Interpol menganggarkan penipuan menggunakan AI mampu menjana keuntungan 4.5 kali ganda lebih tinggi berbanding kaedah tradisional.
“Dengan AI, lebih mudah untuk penjenayah memperdaya dan memanipulasi mangsa melalui teknik kejuruteraan sosial,” katanya.
“Perkembangan ini meletakkan kita dalam ‘perlumbaan senjata’ dengan penjenayah. Apabila mereka mengautomasikan penipuan, kita juga perlu mengautomasikan pengesanan.”
Beliau berucap pada pembukaan persidangan Intelligence-Led Financial Crime Prevention: The Power of Data, Insights and Collaboration anjuran Asian Institute of Chartered Bankers di sini hari ini.
Rasheed berkata sektor kewangan berjaya menghalang transaksi penipuan bernilai kira-kira RM1.9 bilion pada separuh pertama tahun ini, melebihi RM1.2 bilion yang berjaya disekat sepanjang 2025.

Beliau berkata lebih RM37 bilion aset turut berjaya diperoleh semula dalam tempoh lima tahun lalu, manakala beberapa kes jenayah kewangan berprofil tinggi dan kompleks sudah disiasat serta didakwa, termasuk kes membabitkan pelbagai agensi.
“Pencapaian ini membuktikan keberkesanan usaha seluruh negara,” katanya.

Menurut Rasheed, kemajuan Malaysia dalam memerangi jenayah kewangan sepanjang 25 tahun lalu dibina melalui undang-undang dan institusi yang kukuh, selain pemahaman lebih baik mengenai risiko serta pendekatan penyeliaan.

Beliau berkata beberapa pindaan terhadap Akta Pencegahan Pengubahan Wang Haram, Pencegahan Pembiayaan Keganasan, Pencegahan Pembiayaan Aktiviti Terlarang dan Hasil Daripada Aktiviti Haram 2001, bersama penambahbaikan terhadap undang-undang utama lain, telah memperkukuh keupayaan negara untuk menyiasat, mendakwa dan mendapatkan semula aset haram.

Katanya, Malaysia turut menubuhkan beberapa platform bagi penyelarasan dan perkongsian risikan, termasuk Pusat Pencegahan Jenayah Kewangan Nasional, Pusat Respons Scam Kebangsaan, Pasukan Petugas Pelbagai Agensi, Portal Fraud Kebangsaan dan MyFINet.
Rasheed berkata negara kini mempunyai lebih 27,000 institusi pelapor kewangan dan bukan kewangan yang disokong pemantauan berasaskan teknologi.
“Kesemuanya memperkukuh tindak balas bersama kita terhadap jenayah kewangan dan mencerminkan kefahaman bahawa tiada satu institusi mampu menangani ancaman ini secara bersendirian,” katanya.

b7d2fe5ebca6d9b7: PETALING JAYA: Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) akan meneliti keterangan saksi, rakaman CCTV dan bukti lain sebelum menentukan tindakan lanjut berhubung dakwaan Ketua Pengarah Agensi Kawalan dan Perlindungan Sempadan (AKPS), Shuhaily Zain menyerang dua anggota polis.
